keywords.when_to_use: Use for warm, welcoming small homes and neighborhood streets. Great for nostalgic, family-feeling scenes.
keywords.prompt_example: "Craftsman bungalow with a lantern-lit porch, autumn leaves, dusk"

keywords.name: Crane Shot
keywords.definition: The camera sweeps vertically or in an arc from a raised arm, moving between ground level and overhead.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for grand reveals, openings, and moments that deserve scale.
keywords.prompt_example: "crane shot rising from the crowd to reveal the city"

keywords.name: Crayon Picture Book
keywords.definition: A children's book page being drawn as you watch: wax crayon on bumpy paper, color spilling past the lines, every line gently wiggling, and a watercolor wash that sweeps across to reveal hidden white crayon drawings.
keywords.when_to_use: Perfect for kids' stories, family brands and sweet explainers. It reads as made for children, so it can feel too young for grown-up business topics.
keywords.prompt_example: "20-second kids story, crayon picture book animation, wiggly crayon lines drawing a house, watercolor wash revealing hidden stars"

keywords.name: Creative Web Design
keywords.definition: A loud, playful landing page with cartoon characters, comic-book Bangers headlines and bold graphic shapes.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for creative projects, snack and drink launches, kids' events and fun portfolios. Not right for serious services like banking or health.
keywords.prompt_example: "landing page for a cat energy drink, creative web design, cartoon cat mascot, comic headlines"

keywords.name: Cristobal Balenciaga
keywords.definition: Spanish designer Cristóbal Balenciaga (1895-1972) shaped fabric like sculpture: balloon skirts, cocoon coats, loose sack dresses and stiff silks that stand away from the body.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when you want bold, architectural shapes and simple, strong colors. Works best on a plain background where the silhouette can speak.
keywords.prompt_example: "sculptural cocoon coat in the style of cristobal balenciaga, black silk, plain grey studio"

keywords.name: Cross Dissolve
keywords.definition: One image melts into the next; time passing with a soft edge.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for gentle time transitions and memory sequences.
keywords.prompt_example: "cross dissolve from her young face to the old photograph"

keywords.name: Cross-Hatching
keywords.definition: Shading made from layers of crisscrossing pen lines. The more lines stack up, the deeper the shadow.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for engraved, sketchbook or old-newspaper looks. It can get busy, so pair it with a clear subject.
keywords.prompt_example: "cross-hatching pen drawing of an old sailor, dramatic shadows"

keywords.name: Cross-Stitch
keywords.definition: Tiny X-shaped stitches on a grid of fabric, held tight in a wooden hoop. Pictures made one little square at a time.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for folk patterns, cute samplers and homey craft scenes. Stitched letters rarely come out right, so lean on flowers and shapes.
keywords.prompt_example: "cross-stitch of wildflowers in a wooden hoop, embroidery floss scattered around"

keywords.name: Crystal Caverns
keywords.definition: Huge caves filled with giant glowing crystals in every color, sparkling like the inside of a geode.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for fantasy quests, magical hideaways and jewel-like scenes. Name a color or two, or it can turn into a rainbow mess.
keywords.prompt_example: "explorer in crystal caverns, giant purple crystals, soft glow"

keywords.name: Crystal Formations
keywords.definition: Clusters of sharp, glassy crystals growing in points and facets, like inside a geode or a cave. Light sparkles through them.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for magical caves, gem close-ups and fantasy landscapes. Backlight makes them glow from inside.
keywords.prompt_example: "amethyst crystal formations inside a geode, glowing backlight"

keywords.name: Cursor Follower
keywords.definition: A soft coloured circle trails behind the mouse pointer with a little delay, like it is chasing it. It grows when the pointer reaches a button or link, then shrinks back.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it on creative or portfolio sites to add a playful, custom feel. It does nothing on phones and can distract on busy pages, so keep it subtle.
keywords.prompt_example: "Add a soft pink circle that follows my cursor with a slight delay and grows when it is over a button or link"

keywords.name: Cutaway
keywords.definition: A view with part of the outside removed so you can see inside, like a house with the front wall missing.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to show rooms, machines or creatures inside a shell. It can get messy with too many rooms, so name the ones you want.
keywords.prompt_example: "cutaway of a cozy treehouse showing every room"

keywords.name: Cutaway Diagram
keywords.definition: A drawing where a slice of the outside is removed so you can peek inside, like a ship, a house or a volcano cut in half. Every room or layer is on show at once.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to show busy little worlds hiding inside something, such as a dollhouse or a submarine. Very detailed scenes can get crowded, so name only a few rooms.
keywords.prompt_example: "cutaway diagram of a cozy underground rabbit burrow, every room lit"

keywords.name: Cutout Animation
keywords.definition: Characters and scenery made from flat paper pieces, moved around like puppets on a tabletop. You can see the cut edges and the paper grain.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for crafty, folk-tale or collage-style stories. Movement looks a little stiff, which is part of the charm.
keywords.prompt_example: "paper cutout fox chasing the moon over hills, cutout animation"

keywords.name: Cyanotype
keywords.definition: A sun print in deep Prussian blue, where objects laid on special paper leave crisp white ghostly shapes.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for botanical prints, dreamy photos and vintage science looks. Everything turns blue and white, so plan for that.
keywords.prompt_example: "cyanotype of fern leaves and wildflowers, deep blue and white"

keywords.name: Cyber Fairy Grunge
keywords.definition: Fairy grunge wired into the machine: glitching wings, LED moss, digital decay over woodland whimsy.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for tech-touched fantasy characters and glitchy forest scenes.
keywords.prompt_example: "fairy with glitching wings, cyber fairy grunge"

keywords.name: Cyberculture
keywords.definition: Internet-native visual culture: interfaces, avatars, meme textures, and screen-glow life.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for online-life commentary pieces and digital-era portraits.
keywords.prompt_example: "portrait made of browser windows, cyberculture"

keywords.name: Cybergoth
keywords.definition: Goth fused with rave tech: black PVC, neon dreads, goggles, industrial club lighting.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for futuristic club scenes or characters equal parts dark and glowing.
keywords.prompt_example: "dancer portrait, cybergoth style, neon green"

keywords.name: Cybergrunge
keywords.definition: Digital decay aesthetics: corrupted textures, terminal green, grime rendered in pixels.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for dystopian graphics and anti-polish digital art.
keywords.prompt_example: "portrait, cybergrunge, glitch texture"

keywords.name: Cybernetic Punk
keywords.definition: Flesh-and-machine rebellion: visible implants, wires, dystopian grit with attitude.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for hard sci-fi characters and street-level future scenes.
keywords.prompt_example: "portrait with cybernetic arm, cyberpunk street"

keywords.name: Daguerreotype
keywords.definition: The very first popular kind of photograph, from 1839, made on a polished silver mirror. Ghostly, silvery, finely detailed images with a soft glow and dark edges.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for eerie, delicate, museum-like antique portraits. People sat very still for these, so keep poses calm.
keywords.prompt_example: "daguerreotype portrait of a young woman in a lace collar"

keywords.name: Damascus Steel
keywords.definition: Steel with flowing, wavy light and dark patterns rippling across it, like wood grain or water. Each blade is one of a kind.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for knives, swords and close-up texture shots. The pattern is the star, so get close.
keywords.prompt_example: "close-up of a damascus steel blade with wavy patterns, dark background"

keywords.name: Dark Cloud Dashboard UI
keywords.definition: A dark-themed workspace dashboard with neat modular panels, frosted glass-like cards and clear charts, set in IBM Plex Sans.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for analytics tools, monitoring apps and productivity dashboards people look at all day. Too much for a simple brochure site.
keywords.prompt_example: "sales analytics dashboard, dark cloud dashboard ui, charts on dark panels, soft glass cards"

keywords.name: Dark Luxury Web Design
keywords.definition: A high-end, mostly black and grey site with tall, bold Oswald headings and a powerful, expensive feel.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for luxury goods, cars, fitness and premium drinks. Can feel cold or intimidating for friendly brands.
keywords.prompt_example: "website for a luxury watch brand, dark luxury web design, black and grey, tall bold headings"

keywords.name: Dark Tech Keynote
keywords.definition: A software launch film on a near-black stage with a faint grid and soft cool light. A cursor leads, hundreds of notifications and files pile up in rhythm, freeze in silence, then fly into one perfect grid on a single beat.
keywords.when_to_use: Made for software launches, AI tool promos and product feature reels. It is sleek and serious, so it can feel cold for friendly or playful brands.
keywords.prompt_example: "20-second app launch, dark tech keynote animation, notifications piling up on a black stage, then snapping into a perfect grid on the beat"

keywords.name: Dashiki
keywords.definition: A loose, colorful pullover tunic from West Africa with a richly embroidered or printed neckline. Comfortable, roomy and full of bold color.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for portraits, family gatherings and festival scenes. In the 1960s it also became a proud symbol of Black identity in the United States, which can add meaning to your scene.
keywords.prompt_example: "man in a bright blue dashiki with gold embroidered neckline, outdoor market"

keywords.name: Data Chart Animation
keywords.definition: The newsroom way to animate numbers: the axes draw in first, then the data grows into place, and only one thing gets highlighted. Bars start at zero, one color for the star, grey for the rest.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for any number you want people to remember, like growth, price changes or before-and-after comparisons.
keywords.prompt_example: "bar chart grows up from zero, one bar highlighted in red, clean finance chart animation"

keywords.name: Data-Dense Enterprise UI
keywords.definition: A tidy, businesslike screen packed with tables, forms and filters, all lined up in a strict, consistent grid. Plain Plus Jakarta Sans type and quiet colors keep lots of information easy to scan.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for admin panels, back-office tools and apps where people manage lots of records all day. Too busy and serious for a brand or marketing page.
keywords.prompt_example: "order management dashboard for a pet food warehouse, data-dense enterprise ui, tables and filters"

keywords.name: Data Viz Explainer
keywords.definition: Numbers that tell a story: axes draw, bars grow, lines trace and counters tick up to exact values, then everything else dims so the key number stands out.
keywords.when_to_use: Ideal for reports, business explainers and social posts with one key stat. The numbers must be real and correct, and it can feel dry without a clear story.
keywords.prompt_example: "20-second explainer, data viz explainer animation, bars growing and a counter ticking to 72 percent, key bar highlighted"

keywords.name: David Hicks
keywords.definition: English designer (1929-1998) known for bold geometric carpets, hexagon patterns and daring color clashes like hot pink with orange.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for punchy 1960s and 70s rooms full of graphic pattern. Great for color, not for calm.
keywords.prompt_example: "living room with hexagon patterned carpet, pink and orange, David Hicks style"

keywords.name: Day for Night
keywords.definition: Daylight footage graded into moonlight: cool, dim, and slightly unreal.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for stylized night scenes with dreamlike readability.
keywords.prompt_example: "day for night grade, silver-blue orchard"

keywords.name: Decalcomania
keywords.definition: Paint pressed between surfaces and pulled apart, leaving branching accidental textures surrealists loved.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for organic abstract textures and dreamlike landscapes.
keywords.prompt_example: "alien landscape, decalcomania texture"

keywords.name: Deep Focus
keywords.definition: Everything from foreground to horizon stays sharp; layers of story in one frame.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for staging action in depth and letting viewers choose where to look.
keywords.prompt_example: "deep focus, argument in front, children playing far behind"

keywords.name: Defiance
keywords.definition: Standing firm against something bigger: chin up, fists clenched, wind in the hair, looking straight back at the storm or the crowd.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for brave heroes, protest posters and underdog moments. A low angle makes your subject feel even taller and stronger.
keywords.prompt_example: "defiance, young girl facing a giant iron robot, chin raised, rain"

keywords.name: Delftware
keywords.definition: Glossy white Dutch pottery painted in soft cobalt blue: windmills, tulips, ships and little country scenes.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for charming tabletop scenes, tile patterns and cozy Dutch kitchens. Close cousin of blue and white porcelain, but more folksy and storybook.
keywords.prompt_example: "stack of delftware plates and a tulip vase on a sunny windowsill"

keywords.name: Derivative Art
keywords.definition: Art deliberately made from other art: remix, homage, and quotation as method.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for style-mashup experiments and commentary pieces.
keywords.prompt_example: "famous painting reimagined, derivative art remix"

keywords.name: Dieselpunk
keywords.definition: A gritty, alternate past powered by oil and engines, inspired by the 1920s to 1940s. Think riveted airships, smoke and heavy machines.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for moody adventure and alternate history scenes. It is darker and heavier than steampunk, with less brass and more steel.
keywords.prompt_example: "dieselpunk airship over a smoky industrial city, dusk"

keywords.name: Digital Animation
keywords.definition: Rendered motion-picture styling: smooth gradients, expressive characters, animated-feature polish.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for stills that should look like frames from an animated film.
keywords.prompt_example: "animated film still, cozy village morning"

keywords.name: Digital Impressionism
keywords.definition: Impressionist brushwork born digital: loose light-dabbed strokes with modern color freedom.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for painterly scenes with soft edges and glowing light.
keywords.prompt_example: "harbor at dawn, digital impressionism"

keywords.name: Dim Sum
keywords.definition: Little dumplings and buns tucked into round bamboo steamer baskets, often with tea on the side. Delicate, shiny and inviting.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for warm family table scenes and close-up dumpling shots. Pair with steam rising so the baskets feel fresh.
keywords.prompt_example: "bamboo steamer baskets of dim sum dumplings, steam rising, teapot nearby"

keywords.name: Diorama
keywords.definition: A little 3D scene built inside a box or on a base, with a painted backdrop and tiny props, like a museum display.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to frame a whole world in one neat little stage. It works best with one clear setting rather than many things at once.
keywords.prompt_example: "diorama of a rainy forest cabin inside a wooden box"

keywords.name: Disposable Camera
keywords.definition: The look of a cheap throwaway film camera: bright on-camera flash, red eyes, slight blur and grainy colors. Messy, fun and very real.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for party shots, teen memories and casual 90s or Y2K snapshots. It is meant to look imperfect, so do not expect polish.
keywords.prompt_example: "disposable camera photo of friends in a kitchen at night, flash"

keywords.name: Dithered Web Design
keywords.definition: Images and shading made from tiny dot patterns using only a few colors, like an old computer screen or newspaper print. This dotting trick is called dithering, and it looks high contrast and a little nostalgic.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for music, art, tech zines and retro-flavored product pages. The dots can make small details and faces hard to read.
keywords.prompt_example: "album release page, dithered web design, black and white dot pattern photos"

keywords.name: Dolly In
keywords.definition: The camera physically glides toward the subject on a track. Unlike a zoom, the world shifts around them, pulling the viewer closer emotionally.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for slow realizations, rising tension, or drawing attention to a decision on someone's face.
keywords.prompt_example: "slow dolly in on her face as she reads the letter"

keywords.name: Dolly Kei
keywords.definition: Japanese street fashion built from antique European dolls: layered vintage fabrics, religious motifs, dark fairy-tale trims.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for richly layered vintage fashion portraits with a storybook shadow.
keywords.prompt_example: "fashion portrait, dolly kei style"

keywords.name: Dolly Out
keywords.definition: The camera glides away from the subject, revealing context and often leaving them small in their world.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for endings, isolation, or the reveal that changes everything.
keywords.prompt_example: "dolly out from the empty chair, room grows around it"

keywords.name: Dolly Zoom
keywords.definition: Dolly and zoom in opposite directions: the subject stays put while the background stretches. Vertigo in a lens.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for dread, revelation, and the ground falling out from under someone.
keywords.prompt_example: "dolly zoom on his face as he understands"

keywords.name: Doodle
keywords.definition: Playful margin-of-the-notebook drawing: loose, dense, and cheerfully unserious.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for pattern fills, sticker sheets, and hand-drawn warmth.
keywords.prompt_example: "page of doodles, coffee theme"

keywords.name: Doodle Web Design
keywords.definition: A hand-drawn site full of little sketches, wobbly lines and handwritten Delius Swash Caps lettering, like notes in a school notebook.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for kids' brands, teachers, personal blogs and friendly small shops. Can look messy on pages packed with information.
keywords.prompt_example: "website for a kids' art club, doodle web design, hand-drawn arrows and stars"

keywords.name: Doodles on Photo
keywords.definition: A real photo with playful white or colored doodles drawn over it, like hearts, wings, sparkles and little faces.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for fun social posts, cheeky portraits and pet photos. Keep the doodles simple, busy drawings can bury the photo.
keywords.prompt_example: "photo of a corgi with white doodle wings and a crown"

keywords.name: Dorothea Lange
keywords.definition: (1895-1965) American documentary photographer known for honest, tender portraits of working families during the Great Depression. Plain black and white, weathered faces, quiet strength.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for serious, human portraits with an old American feel. The style is about dignity, not drama, so keep subjects respectful.
keywords.prompt_example: "farm worker resting by a truck, 1930s, in the style of Dorothea Lange"

keywords.name: Dorothy Draper
keywords.definition: American decorator (1889-1969) known for big, happy glamour: black and white checkerboard floors, huge cabbage rose prints, bright pink and green, and giant white plaster scrolls.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for bold, cheerful hotel lobbies and dramatic rooms. Not for minimal or quiet scenes.
keywords.prompt_example: "hotel lobby, black and white checkered floor, pink and green walls, Dorothy Draper style"

keywords.name: Dorothy of Oz
keywords.definition: The Kansas farm girl from the original 1900 book, in a blue and white checked gingham dress with her little dog Toto. In the book her magic shoes are silver, not red. Describe the book version.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for whimsical journeys, colorful fantasy lands and yellow brick roads. Mention 'silver shoes' and 'original book illustration' to stay true to the book.
keywords.prompt_example: "dorothy of oz from the 1900 book, silver shoes, toto, yellow brick road, original book illustration"

keywords.name: Double Exposure
keywords.definition: Two pictures blended into one, like a person's silhouette filled with a forest or a city. Dreamy and poetic, as if memories overlap.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for album covers, posters and emotional portraits. Keep both images simple, or the blend turns to mush.
keywords.prompt_example: "double exposure of a woman's profile and a pine forest"

keywords.name: Dramatic Web Design
keywords.definition: A theatrical site with strong contrast, huge images, unusual layouts and big Outfit headlines that feel like a movie poster.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for films, fashion, theater and big product reveals. Visitors looking for quick information may find it slow or confusing.
keywords.prompt_example: "website for a theater premiere, dramatic web design, black stage, single spotlight on the title"

keywords.name: Dreamscape
keywords.definition: A landscape built from dream logic: floating islands, impossible skies, soft physics.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when reality is optional. Great for surreal art and emotional storytelling.
keywords.prompt_example: "pastel dreamscape with floating staircases and slow clouds"

keywords.name: Dropdown Menu
keywords.definition: A box that opens a short list of choices when you click it. Moving over the list highlights each option, and the one you pick shows in the box.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it when there are several choices but only room for one box. With just two or three options, plain buttons are quicker to use.
keywords.prompt_example: "Add a dropdown menu for picking a style that opens with a smooth drop, highlights the option under the mouse and shows my choice in the box"

keywords.name: Dry Brush
keywords.definition: A nearly dry brush dragged across paper or canvas, so the paint skips and leaves scratchy, broken streaks. Rough, airy and full of texture.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for wind, grass, weathered wood and rugged landscapes. It's less suited to smooth skin or glossy surfaces.
keywords.prompt_example: "wild grass on a windy hill, dry brush painting"

keywords.name: Dual Kawaii
keywords.definition: Split-personality cute: one half sweet pastels, the other half dark or edgy, in a single design.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for character designs that need contrast or before-and-after energy in one frame.
keywords.prompt_example: "character sheet, dual kawaii style, half pastel half black"

keywords.name: Dunhuang Mural
keywords.definition: Buddhist cave paintings from the Silk Road in China: earthy red backgrounds, mineral greens and blues, flying celestial figures trailing long ribbons, and paint worn and flaking with age.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for graceful, spiritual scenes, flowing fabric and anything that should feel ancient, sacred and softly faded.
keywords.prompt_example: "celestial dancer with flowing ribbons, dunhuang mural, faded mineral colors"

keywords.name: Duochrome
keywords.definition: A finish that shifts between two colors as you move, like a beetle shell or shimmery eyeshadow going from purple to green.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for cars, makeup, beetles and futuristic fashion. It is related to iridescent, but duochrome sticks to just two colors.
keywords.prompt_example: "duochrome sports car, purple to green color shift, studio"

keywords.name: Dust Particles
keywords.definition: Tiny specks floating in the air, glowing where a beam of light catches them. They make a room feel still, old and lived-in.
keywords.when_to_use: Use in sunny windows, attics, libraries and quiet moments. They only show up well when there's a strong beam of light to catch them.
keywords.prompt_example: "old library in the morning, dust particles in a sunbeam"

keywords.name: Dusty Rose
keywords.definition: A muted, grayish pink, softer and calmer than bubblegum. Like old roses or faded silk.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for gentle, romantic and vintage looks. If you want pink that pops, choose a brighter pink instead.
keywords.prompt_example: "dusty rose bridesmaid dresses in a garden"

keywords.name: Dutch Angle
keywords.definition: The horizon tilts off-level; the world is subtly, deliberately wrong.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for unease, disorientation, and villain energy.
keywords.prompt_example: "dutch angle as the lights flicker in the corridor"

keywords.name: Early CGI
keywords.definition: The look of 1990s computer graphics: shiny plastic surfaces, chrome balls, checkerboard floors with perfect reflections and a slightly toy-like, too-clean finish.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for retro tech nostalgia, music-video throwbacks and playful 3D scenes that wink at the dawn of computer art.
keywords.prompt_example: "chrome sphere on a checkerboard floor, early cgi, 1993 render"

keywords.name: Eco Art
keywords.definition: Environment-centered art practice: living materials, land collaboration, ecological storytelling.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for nature-advocacy concepts and land-based installations.
keywords.prompt_example: "river cleaned into an artwork, eco art installation"

keywords.name: Editorial
keywords.definition: Magazine-style photography: intentional, styled, confident. Every element placed on purpose.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for fashion, products, and brand imagery that should feel premium.
keywords.prompt_example: "editorial photo of a woman in a structured coat, studio"

keywords.name: Editorial HUD
keywords.definition: A precise magazine page come to life: giant narrow headlines, fine grid lines and a running on-screen readout like a timecode and progress bar, on pastel backgrounds. Each cut zooms or wipes through the thing you are already looking at.
keywords.when_to_use: Great for how-it-works explainers, step-by-step processes and behind-the-scenes reels. It looks smart but busy, so it needs a clear script to stay readable.
keywords.prompt_example: "20-second how it works reel, editorial hud animation, giant headline, hairline grid, timecode in the corner, zooming through each step"

keywords.name: Editorial Poster Web Design
keywords.definition: A warm, confident site that looks like a graphic poster, alternating cream and burnt orange sections with an amber accent and bold Chakra Petch headings.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for agencies, events, food and lifestyle brands that want graphic punch with warmth. The strong orange may clash with cool brand colors.
keywords.prompt_example: "website for a jazz festival, editorial poster web design, cream and burnt orange stripes"

keywords.name: Editorial Web Design
keywords.definition: A magazine-style site with refined Gelasio serif type (letters with small feet at the ends), tidy columns and a calm, elegant reading feel.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for blogs, online magazines, recipe sites and long stories. Less suited to busy apps full of buttons.
keywords.prompt_example: "food magazine website, editorial web design, large serif headline, two text columns"

keywords.name: Edmund Dulac
keywords.definition: (1882-1953) French-born British illustrator of fairy tales and the Arabian Nights. Dreamy midnight blues, glowing moons and jewel-like details.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for magical night scenes, palaces and starry fairy tales. Lean into deep blue for his classic look.
keywords.prompt_example: "princess on a moonlit balcony over a sleeping city, in the style of Edmund Dulac"

keywords.name: Edvard Munch
keywords.definition: (1863-1944) Norwegian painter of The Scream, known for wavy, emotional landscapes and figures soaked in anxious feeling. Blood-orange skies and swirling lines.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for haunting, emotional, unsettling scenes. It is a heavy mood, not a happy one.
keywords.prompt_example: "lonely figure on a bridge under a blood-orange sky, in the style of Edvard Munch"

keywords.name: Edwardian Fashion
keywords.definition: Dress from the early 1900s: high lace collars, puffy blouses, long sweeping skirts and enormous hats piled with flowers and feathers. Elegant, layered and very ladylike.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for garden parties, grand hotels and early 1900s city streets. It can blur into Victorian, so add the decade if you need it exact.
keywords.prompt_example: "edwardian fashion, woman in a lace blouse and wide feathered hat, seaside promenade, 1905"

keywords.name: Egg Chair
keywords.definition: A curved, swiveling lounge chair shaped like a hollow egg with the front scooped out, so you sit tucked inside it.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for retro modern lounges, hotel lobbies and sci-fi homes. A fun single hero piece.
keywords.prompt_example: "bright red egg chair in a white lobby, soft daylight"

keywords.name: Egyptian Tomb Painting
keywords.definition: Ancient Egyptian wall art: figures with side-on faces and front-facing eyes, flat bright colors, crisp outlines and rows of hieroglyphs in neat bands.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for stylized storytelling scenes, mythic portraits and any subject that should feel ceremonial and ancient.
keywords.prompt_example: "cat sipping tea at a low table, egyptian tomb painting, hieroglyph border"

keywords.name: Elderly
keywords.definition: An older person, often in their seventies or beyond, with lined skin, silver or thinning hair and hands that show a long life. Shown with dignity, warmth and character.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to bring older people into your scenes as full, active people: gardeners, dancers, teachers, grandparents. Name an activity so they are doing, not just sitting.
keywords.prompt_example: "elderly man with silver beard tending tomatoes in a sunny allotment"

keywords.name: Elizabethan Fashion
keywords.definition: English court dress from the late 1500s: huge starched lace ruffs around the neck, stiff jeweled bodices, wide skirts held out by hoops, and rich brocade sewn with pearls.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for royal portraits, historical drama and Shakespeare-style scenes. Very ornate, so keep the rest of the scene simple.
keywords.prompt_example: "portrait of a noblewoman in elizabethan fashion, white lace ruff, pearl-studded gown"

keywords.name: Elsa Schiaparelli
keywords.definition: Italian-born designer Elsa Schiaparelli (1890-1973) made fashion playful and surreal: shocking pink, trick-of-the-eye sweaters, lobster prints, hats shaped like shoes and wild jeweled buttons.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for witty, dreamlike fashion that breaks the rules. Add one surreal detail to the prompt so the AI knows where to play.
keywords.prompt_example: "surreal evening gown in the style of elsa schiaparelli, shocking pink, lobster print, gilded salon"

keywords.name: Elsie de Wolfe
keywords.definition: American decorator (1859-1950) often called the first professional interior designer. She swapped dark Victorian rooms for light walls, mirrors, garden trellis and pretty chintz.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for airy, feminine, garden-inspired rooms with an early 1900s feel. Keeps things soft and fresh rather than grand.
keywords.prompt_example: "sunroom with green trellis walls and chintz chairs, Elsie de Wolfe style"

keywords.name: Embroidered Photo
keywords.definition: A printed photo with real-looking stitches sewn right into it, adding thread flowers, halos or colored patterns.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for handmade, nostalgic and quirky portraits. Stitch detail works best when large and simple, tiny stitches can smudge.
keywords.prompt_example: "vintage portrait with embroidered flower crown, colorful thread"

keywords.name: Embroidery
keywords.definition: Pictures and patterns stitched with colored thread onto fabric, with raised, glossy stitches you can almost feel.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for cozy, handmade looks on clothes, hoops and patches. Great for flowers, animals and lettering.
keywords.prompt_example: "embroidery hoop with wildflowers and a bee, linen fabric, close-up"

keywords.name: Emerald Cut
keywords.definition: A rectangle-shaped gem cut with clipped corners and long, step-like facets. Instead of sparkle, it gives clean flashes of light like a hall of mirrors.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for elegant, vintage-feeling rings and pendants, with any stone, not just emeralds. Say the stone and the setting for best results.
keywords.prompt_example: "emerald cut diamond engagement ring, platinum setting, soft window light"

keywords.name: Emo
keywords.definition: Early-2000s mall goth mood: black layers, side-swept fringe, checkerboard, eyeliner, and feelings.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for nostalgic 2000s portraits or moody youth-culture scenes with a soft heart.
keywords.prompt_example: "portrait of a teenager, emo aesthetic, 2005"

keywords.name: Empty State
keywords.definition: What a page shows when there is nothing in it yet: a friendly little drawing, a short message and a button to get started. It turns a blank space into a clear next step.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it on any list, inbox or gallery that can be empty, especially for brand new users. Keep the words short and the button obvious.
keywords.prompt_example: "When the saved picks list is empty, show a simple line drawing of an open box with a heart, the words Nothing here yet and an Add first pick button."

keywords.name: Encaustic Art
keywords.definition: Painting with molten pigmented wax: luminous layers, fused textures, ancient technique.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for richly textured abstract or portrait surfaces with depth and glow.
keywords.prompt_example: "seascape, encaustic painting, layered wax"

keywords.name: English Country House
keywords.definition: Faded chintz sofas, floral curtains, worn rugs, dogs by the fire, oil portraits and piles of books. Comfortable, a bit shabby and full of history.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for cozy old manor rooms that feel lived in for generations. Best when things look slightly worn rather than brand new.
keywords.prompt_example: "English country house drawing room, chintz sofa, fireplace, rainy afternoon"

keywords.name: Epic Fantasy Map
keywords.definition: The hand-drawn world map at the front of a fantasy novel: mountains drawn as little peaks, winding rivers, sea monsters in the corners and old-style lettering.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for worldbuilding, book covers and game art. Place names will often be invented gibberish, so ask for few labels or none.
keywords.prompt_example: "epic fantasy map of an island kingdom, ink on parchment, sea serpents"

keywords.name: Establishing Shot
keywords.definition: An opening view that tells the audience where and when they are before anything happens.
keywords.when_to_use: Use at scene starts and location changes.
keywords.prompt_example: "establishing shot, rain-soaked neon street, midnight"

keywords.name: Etching
keywords.definition: A print made from lines scratched into a metal plate and bitten with acid, so the picture is built from fine crosshatched lines.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for old book illustrations, maps and detailed vintage scenes. Mostly black and white, with tiny delicate lines.
keywords.prompt_example: "etching of an old harbor town, fine crosshatching, sepia ink"

keywords.name: Ethereal
keywords.definition: Light, airy, and not quite of this world. Glow, softness, and a floating feeling.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to lift any scene toward the magical. One of the strongest single-word mood shifters.
keywords.prompt_example: "ethereal portrait, soft glow, floating fabric"

keywords.name: Eucalyptus
keywords.definition: Round, coin-shaped or long leaves in a soft silvery blue-green, often tied in loose bunches. Fresh and calm.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for wedding florals, spa-like scenes and gentle green palettes. A few sprigs soften almost any still life.
keywords.prompt_example: "bunch of eucalyptus in a glass vase, soft daylight, linen backdrop"

keywords.name: Euphoria
keywords.definition: Pure, bursting joy: arms thrown wide, heads tipped back laughing, color and light everywhere. The kind of moment you want to live in.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for celebrations, music, festivals and big wins. It can tip into chaos, so give it one clear subject to hold onto.
keywords.prompt_example: "euphoria, dancers throwing colored powder at sunset festival"

keywords.name: Exploded Product Animation
keywords.definition: A clean tech reveal where a product separates layer by layer and floats apart in a calm studio. The camera glides between the pieces, thin lines link each part to a label, then it all clicks back together.
keywords.when_to_use: Ideal for gadget launches, how-it's-made explainers and spec breakdowns. It needs a product with real layers inside, so it does little for soft or simple items.
keywords.prompt_example: "12-second gadget reveal, exploded product animation, headphones separating into layers with white label lines, then clicking back together"

keywords.name: Exploded View
keywords.definition: An object pulled apart into its pieces, all floating in order, so you can see how it fits together.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for gadgets, sneakers, burgers and anything fun to take apart. The parts may not be accurate, so treat it as art, not instructions.
keywords.prompt_example: "exploded view of a cheeseburger, studio light, white background"

keywords.name: Expressionist Architecture
keywords.definition: Buildings as emotion: sweeping sculptural forms, distorted brick, structures that feel.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for dramatic architectural scenes beyond rational modernism.
keywords.prompt_example: "concert hall, expressionist architecture"

keywords.name: Expressive Web Design
keywords.definition: A lively, personality-packed site with bold colors, playful graphics and shifting layouts, all set in the typewriter-like IBM Plex Mono font.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for creative studios, events and youthful brands that still need clear structure. Can tire the eye if every section is loud.
keywords.prompt_example: "website for a design school open day, expressive web design, bold color blocks, playful shapes"

keywords.name: Extreme Close-Up
keywords.definition: A single detail fills everything: an eye, a trembling hand, a turning key.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for tension details and sensory intimacy.
keywords.prompt_example: "extreme close-up of the match striking"

keywords.name: Extreme Wide Shot
keywords.definition: The subject is tiny in a vast environment; landscape as the loudest voice.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for openings, isolation, and scale that words can't carry.
keywords.prompt_example: "extreme wide shot, lone figure crossing the salt flat"

keywords.name: Eye Level
keywords.definition: The camera sits at the subject's eye height, looking straight at them.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when you want the angle to feel neutral and honest.
keywords.prompt_example: "eye-level shot of her across the kitchen table"

keywords.name: Fade In on Scroll
keywords.definition: Cards and sections rise a little and fade into view one after another as they enter the screen. The page seems to reveal itself as you read down.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it to make a long list of cards or features feel lively and easy to follow. Do not hide important content behind it, since slow devices may show it late.
keywords.prompt_example: "Make each card rise slightly and fade in, one after another, when it scrolls into view"

keywords.name: Fade to Black
keywords.definition: The picture fades away to black.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for endings, chapter breaks and deliberate pauses. Not between every scene.
keywords.prompt_example: "final shot fades to black"

keywords.name: Fairy Academia
keywords.definition: Dark academia's bookish charm with mushrooms, moth wings, and forest-library light.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for scholarly-magical scenes: old books, candlelight, and something watching from the ferns.
keywords.prompt_example: "reading nook in a hollow tree, fairy academia"

keywords.name: Fairy Grunge
keywords.definition: Woodland whimsy dragged through the mud: fairy wings and lace with dirt, moss, and distressed layers.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when you want magic that looks lived-in rather than polished.
keywords.prompt_example: "forest wanderer, fairy grunge aesthetic"

keywords.name: Fairy Tale
keywords.definition: The old storybook world of enchanted woods, tiny cottages, talking animals and castles on hills. Soft, a little dark, and full of once upon a time.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for magical children's book scenes and dreamy portraits. Add 'dark' if you want the older, stranger versions of these tales.
keywords.prompt_example: "fairy tale cottage in a mossy forest, storybook illustration"

keywords.name: Falling Backward
keywords.definition: A body tipping back into the air, arms loose, as if falling into water, a bed of flowers or a dream. It feels like letting go.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for surreal, dreamy and trust-falling moments. Show what they are falling into, so it reads as peaceful rather than scary.
keywords.prompt_example: "woman falling backward into a pool of floating petals, overhead view"

keywords.name: Falling Blocks Game Web Design
keywords.definition: A classic block-puzzle game look with chunky colorful tiles stacking up, bold comic Bangers headings and compact, high-energy layouts.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for game sites, toy brands, puzzle apps and playful events. Busy blocks can crowd out text if you use too many.
keywords.prompt_example: "website for a toy store, falling blocks game web design, colorful stacked tiles, bold headings"

keywords.name: Fantasy Game Web Design
keywords.definition: A rich, game-inspired site with deep jewel colors, ornate New Rocker lettering and grand, adventure-style visuals like a fantasy game launcher.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for games, tabletop adventures, fantasy books and events. Too ornate for everyday businesses.
keywords.prompt_example: "website for a dragon adventure game, fantasy game web design, gold lettering, deep purple"

keywords.name: Fast Orbit Into Crash Zoom
keywords.definition: A tight, quick circle around the subject that makes it seem to spin, ending in a hard zoom.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it for spins, a hero turning, or a car drifting. Fast circles can warp faces and hands, so check the result closely.
keywords.prompt_example: "a fast, tight 280 degree orbit around a dancer mid-spin, ending in a crash zoom onto her face"

keywords.name: Fauvism
keywords.definition: Wild early-modern color: nature painted in unapologetic, non-realistic hues.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for joyful high-saturation landscapes and portraits.
keywords.prompt_example: "harbor scene, fauvism, wild color"

keywords.name: Faux Naif Art
keywords.definition: Trained artists painting deliberately childlike; sophistication wearing innocence.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for knowing-whimsical scenes with naive charm and sly craft.
keywords.prompt_example: "city street, faux naif painting"

keywords.name: Felt and Fabric
keywords.definition: A cozy world made of felt shapes with fuzzy edges and hand stitching on a fabric backdrop. Stitches sew themselves on and each piece hops into place in jerky stop motion, like a hand nudged it between frames.
keywords.when_to_use: Perfect for warm, friendly explainers, kids' content and small handmade brands. The charm comes from its slow, homemade feel, so it is a poor fit for sleek tech or luxury.
keywords.prompt_example: "10-second product reel, felt and fabric animation, stitched shapes hopping in on a linen backdrop"

keywords.name: Femme Fatale
keywords.definition: The glamorous, mysterious woman of old crime films, calm and clever, whose charm hides danger. Think sharp tailoring, window-blind shadows and a knowing look.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for noir scenes and moody, stylish character portraits. It's a well-worn type, so give her a goal or a job to make her more than a cliche.
keywords.prompt_example: "femme fatale in a trench coat, rainy street, noir lighting"

keywords.name: Ferns
keywords.definition: Soft, feathery fronds that curl open from little spirals, filling shady forest floors in layers of green.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for lush woodland scenes, fairy worlds and green, shady corners. They love misty, soft light.
keywords.prompt_example: "forest floor of ferns, morning mist, soft green light"

keywords.name: Ferrofluid
keywords.definition: A black, magnetic liquid that rises into spiky, hedgehog-like shapes when a magnet comes near. Strange, shiny and hypnotic.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for weird, futuristic close-ups and satisfying motion. It looks best in video, where the spikes grow and melt back.
keywords.prompt_example: "black ferrofluid forming spikes on a mirror, studio light, macro"

keywords.name: Field Guide Page
keywords.definition: A page from a naturalist's guidebook, with neat painted birds, bugs or mushrooms, each with a small label and notes. It feels patient, curious and outdoorsy.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when you want a collection of creatures or plants shown side by side. Great for made-up species too, if you want a gentle fantasy feel.
keywords.prompt_example: "field guide page of imaginary forest moths, watercolor, labeled"

keywords.name: Figurative Expressionism
keywords.definition: Human figures painted with raw, emotional distortion; feeling over anatomy.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for intense portraits where the paint carries the psychology.
keywords.prompt_example: "portrait, figurative expressionism, heavy impasto"

keywords.name: Figure-Ground Illusion
keywords.definition: A picture you can read two ways, like a white vase that is also two dark faces looking at each other.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for clever posters, logos and dreamy portraits. It works best with two flat colors and simple shapes.
keywords.prompt_example: "figure-ground illusion, two faces forming a vase, black and white"

keywords.name: Filigree
keywords.definition: Jewelry made from tiny twisted threads of gold or silver, curled into delicate lace-like patterns full of little open spaces.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for heirloom, fantasy and wedding jewelry with lots of fine detail. Works best in close-up; very small filigree can turn to mush.
keywords.prompt_example: "silver filigree earrings with tiny swirls and loops, close-up on linen"

keywords.name: Film Photography
keywords.definition: The analog look: gentle grain, imperfect color, soft highlights. Warmth digital can't fake.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for nostalgia and humanity. Makes AI images feel less AI.
keywords.prompt_example: "film photography of a seaside town, slight grain"

keywords.name: Filter Chips
keywords.definition: A row of small rounded buttons, called chips, that you tap to narrow down what is shown. Picked chips fill with colour and the grid below rearranges to match.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it to let people sort a gallery or shop by type in one tap. Too many chips in a row becomes hard to scan, so keep it to the main groups.
keywords.prompt_example: "Add filter chips above my gallery grid, where tapping a chip fills it pink and the cards smoothly shuffle to show only matching items"

keywords.name: Fire
keywords.definition: Flickering orange and yellow flames that glow, dance and throw warm light on everything near them.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for warmth, danger or drama, from a cozy hearth to a wild blaze. It also works as a strong light source in dark scenes.
keywords.prompt_example: "campfire in a dark forest, flames lighting the faces around it"

keywords.name: First Snow
keywords.definition: Light, fresh snowfall that hasn't been walked through yet. Clean, quiet, hopeful.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for winter softness without harshness, and for scenes about new beginnings.
keywords.prompt_example: "red postbox under first snow, early morning"

keywords.name: Flamenco
keywords.definition: A fiery Spanish dance with swirling ruffled skirts, stamping heels, proud posture and sharp hand movements. Passion in motion.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for dramatic, colorful scenes with lots of movement and feeling. The flying skirt looks amazing in video.
keywords.prompt_example: "flamenco dancer in a red ruffled dress, skirt mid-swirl, warm spotlight"

keywords.name: Flash Match Montage
keywords.definition: A flash of light opens a quick chain of cuts, with a round shape in the same spot each time.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it to open a montage or show a memory. Pick one simple shape, like a moon, a clock or a plate, so the matches line up.
keywords.prompt_example: "a flash fills the frame, then a chain of match cuts, a full moon, a clock face, a dinner plate, each the same size and position, ending on a kitchen at dawn"

keywords.name: Flash to White
keywords.definition: The frame blows out to white from a real light, then fades into the next shot.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for memories, revelations and impact.
keywords.prompt_example: "a camera flash fires and the white fades into the next scene"

keywords.name: Flat Lay
keywords.definition: A photo taken straight down at things arranged on a table or floor. Casual, styled and very social media.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for food, fashion outfits, stationery and product moods. Unlike knolling, it can be loose and artful rather than strictly lined up.
keywords.prompt_example: "flat lay of a cozy breakfast, linen napkin, morning light"

keywords.name: Flat Science Explainer
keywords.definition: Bright flat shapes with no outlines in a softly glowing world, where the camera zooms between the tiny and the enormous, from a single cell to a whole planet.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for science, space, biology and big-picture ideas where scale is the story.
keywords.prompt_example: "camera zooms from a drop of seawater into a glowing diatom, flat science explainer, no outlines"

keywords.name: Flat Vector Illustration
keywords.definition: Today's clean digital illustration: solid color shapes with no outlines, a soft grain texture, friendly characters in expressive poses and plenty of breathing room.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for explainers, app and brand graphics, editorial spots and characters that should feel modern and approachable.
keywords.prompt_example: "woman watering plants on a sunny balcony, flat vector illustration, soft grain texture"

keywords.name: Flat Web Design
keywords.definition: Everything is flat and two-dimensional: no shadows, no shiny effects, no textures, just bright solid colors and clean Inter type.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for apps, icons, explainers and fast, simple sites. Can feel a little generic without strong illustrations.
keywords.prompt_example: "recycling guide website, flat web design, solid bright colors, simple icons"

keywords.name: Floating Action Button
keywords.definition: A round button that floats in the bottom corner of a phone screen for the main thing you do in the app, usually with a plus sign. Tapping it can turn the plus into an X and fan out a few smaller choices.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it in mobile apps where one action matters most, like writing a new note. One per screen is plenty, and make sure it never covers important content.
keywords.prompt_example: "Add a round pink plus button in the bottom right corner of the mobile app that rotates into an X when tapped and fans out three small buttons for note, photo and voice."

keywords.name: Floating Embers
keywords.definition: Glowing orange sparks drifting up from a fire into the dark. Warm, a little dangerous, and a little magical.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for campfires, forges, battles and moody fantasy. They need darkness around them, so they fade away in bright daylight.
keywords.prompt_example: "blacksmith at the forge, floating embers, dark workshop"

keywords.name: Florence Knoll
keywords.definition: American architect and designer (1917-2019) who shaped the tidy mid-century office: open plans, low sleek sofas, slim steel legs, neat grids and calm blocks of color.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for clean, organized 1950s offices and modern lounges. Feels polished rather than cozy.
keywords.prompt_example: "1950s executive office, low sleek sofa, walnut desk, Florence Knoll style"

keywords.name: Flour Dust
keywords.definition: A soft cloud of flour puffing up from hands, dough or a counter. Floating specks catch the light like snow.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for baking scenes and homey kitchen moments. A beam of side light makes the dust glow.
keywords.prompt_example: "baker clapping floured hands, flour dust in a sunbeam, rustic kitchen"

keywords.name: Flowchart
keywords.definition: Boxes and arrows that walk you through steps or choices, one after another. Clear, friendly and easy to follow at a glance.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for how-to graphics, explainers and playful decision charts. Keep the words short, because AI often scrambles long labels.
keywords.prompt_example: "hand-drawn flowchart for choosing a houseplant, pastel boxes and arrows"

keywords.name: Fog
keywords.definition: Thick soft mist that hides distance and mutes color. The world becomes quiet and mysterious.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to simplify busy scenes, add mystery, or make light rays visible.
keywords.prompt_example: "lone streetlamp in heavy fog"

keywords.name: Folk Art
keywords.definition: Traditional community art forms: handmade, decorative, passed down rather than taught in academies.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for warm cultural scenes and handcraft-textured illustration.
keywords.prompt_example: "painted wooden horses, folk art"

keywords.name: Follow Shot
keywords.definition: The camera follows behind someone as they move.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to take the viewer on the journey with your character.
keywords.prompt_example: "follow shot behind her as she walks into the crowd"

keywords.name: Forced Perspective
keywords.definition: A trick where something near the camera lines up with something far away, so a person seems to pinch the moon or hold up a tower.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for playful travel shots and giant or tiny effects. It needs a clear near subject and far subject, so describe both.
keywords.prompt_example: "forced perspective, girl pinching the full moon between her fingers"

keywords.name: Foreground Wipe
keywords.definition: Something passes right in front of the lens and, as it clears, the scene behind has changed.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for a smooth one-take feel. One of the easiest transitions to get right in AI video.
keywords.prompt_example: "a blurred figure walks across the lens; as they clear frame we are in a new street"

keywords.name: Found Object Art
keywords.definition: Everyday objects recontextualized as art, duchampian mischief included.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for conceptual still lifes and sculpture from the junk drawer.
keywords.prompt_example: "sculpture of a bird from spoons, found object art"

keywords.name: Found Text Art
keywords.definition: Compositions built from scavenged words: newspaper cutouts, old letters, ransom-note poetry.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for typographic collage and text-driven emotional pieces.
keywords.prompt_example: "poem made of newspaper cutouts, found text art"

keywords.name: FPV Drone
keywords.definition: Fast first-person drone flight: the camera is the drone, diving and banking through space.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for adrenaline, and for paths no person could ever fly.
keywords.prompt_example: "FPV drone dives off the cliff and skims the waves"

keywords.name: Frame Within a Frame
keywords.definition: Using a doorway, arch, window or branches to make a natural frame around the subject inside the picture.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to pull the eye straight to your subject and add depth. Name the frame, like framed by a stone archway.
keywords.prompt_example: "lighthouse framed by a stone archway, golden hour"

keywords.name: Frank Lloyd Wright
keywords.definition: American architect (1867-1959) whose houses hug the land with long, low roofs, warm wood, stone and bands of windows. His most famous home sits right over a waterfall.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for calm, earthy homes that feel grown from the landscape. Works best for houses and cabins, less so for city towers.
keywords.prompt_example: "house built over a forest waterfall, Frank Lloyd Wright style, autumn"

keywords.name: Frankenstein's Creature
keywords.definition: The being from the 1818 novel: very tall, with yellowish skin, flowing black hair, watery eyes and dark lips, gentle and well-spoken at first. No neck bolts or flat head, those came from later films. Describe the book version.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for tragic, thoughtful gothic portraits that feel more human than monster. Say 'as described in the 1818 novel' to steer away from the movie look.
keywords.prompt_example: "frankenstein's creature from the 1818 novel, reading by firelight in a snowy hut, melancholy"

keywords.name: Freckles
keywords.definition: Small, scattered brown spots across the nose, cheeks and shoulders. They add warmth and personality to a face.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to make portraits feel natural and less airbrushed. Say 'light freckles' if they come out too heavy.
keywords.prompt_example: "portrait of a smiling teenager with freckles, soft window light"

keywords.name: Freelensing
keywords.definition: Taking the lens off the camera and holding it loosely in front. Only a thin slice stays sharp, and the rest melts into blur and glowing haze.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for soft, romantic portraits and flowers. It is unpredictable on purpose, so try a few versions.
keywords.prompt_example: "freelensing portrait of a bride in a meadow, thin slice of focus, hazy light"

keywords.name: Freeze Frame
keywords.definition: The picture freezes on a peak moment, then the next shot starts from that same pose.
keywords.when_to_use: Use as a pattern break, a punchline or a 'that's me' moment.
keywords.prompt_example: "she leaps; the frame freezes at the top of the jump"

keywords.name: Friendly Pastel Web Design
keywords.definition: A gentle, welcoming site with rounded corners, plenty of breathing room and soft pastel colors, with headings in Noto Serif Display.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for wellness, baby, community and beginner-friendly brands. May feel too soft for edgy or high-tech products.
keywords.prompt_example: "website for a baby sleep coach, friendly pastel web design, rounded cards, mint and peach"

keywords.name: From Behind
keywords.definition: The subject seen from the back, looking out at what they see. It invites you to stand in their shoes.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for travel, wonder and quiet, thoughtful moods. Faces stay hidden, which is handy when you do not want a face at all.
keywords.prompt_example: "woman seen from behind looking over a misty valley, fog"

keywords.name: Frutiger Aero
keywords.definition: The hopeful tech look of the late 2000s: sky-blue gradients, glossy see-through bubbles, water droplets, fresh green leaves and shiny aqua buttons. Bubbles float up, wobble and pop to reveal text or icons.
keywords.when_to_use: Lovely for nostalgic, feel-good tech reels, wellness apps and eco brands. Its sunny optimism can feel dated or sugary if your message is serious.
keywords.prompt_example: "10-second app promo, frutiger aero animation, glossy bubbles rising over a sky-blue gradient and popping to reveal icons"

keywords.name: Full Shot
keywords.definition: The whole person from head to feet, nothing cut off.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to show an outfit, a pose, a dance move or a full action.
keywords.prompt_example: "full shot of the dancer mid-leap"

keywords.name: Funk Art
keywords.definition: Irreverent 1960s California movement: crude, funny, ceramic-heavy anti-elegance.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for playful, rude-on-purpose sculptural subjects.
keywords.prompt_example: "ceramic sculpture of a hamburger, funk art"

keywords.name: Furry Art
keywords.definition: Anthropomorphic animal character art with expressive, stylized designs.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for anthro character commissions-style renders and mascot design.
keywords.prompt_example: "anthropomorphic fox character, furry art style"

keywords.name: Futuristic Web Design
keywords.definition: A sleek, forward-looking site with tech-style Audiowide headings, clean modern layouts and a sharp, inventive feel.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for tech startups, gadgets, science and future-themed events. Can feel cold for handmade or cozy brands.
keywords.prompt_example: "product page for smart headphones, futuristic web design, silver and black, glowing lines"

keywords.name: Game Show Flat
keywords.definition: A sunny daytime TV quiz: flat shapes with thick outlines and hard shadows on striped and sunburst sets. Every pop, tick, buzz and ding lands on one fast beat, with quick cuts and a snap zoom on the big reaction.
keywords.when_to_use: Made for quizzes, polls, myth versus fact reels and audience questions. It is loud and fast, so it is wrong for gentle or emotional topics.
keywords.prompt_example: "15-second quiz reel, game show flat animation, answer tiles popping in on a sunburst set, buzzer and snap zoom on the reveal"

keywords.name: -gaze
keywords.definition: Taken from shoegaze, a hazy, dreamy style of rock music. Adding -gaze suggests soft blur, washed-out color and a floaty, half-remembered feeling.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for dreamy, out-of-focus moods and album-cover style art. It blurs things on purpose, so it's not for crisp detail.
keywords.prompt_example: "dreamgaze field at dusk, soft blur, faded pink light"

keywords.name: Generative Particles
keywords.definition: Art made by rules: thousands of tiny particles drift on invisible currents leaving fine trails, then gather into a word or shape on the beat, hold for a breath and dissolve back into the flow.
keywords.when_to_use: Great for tech brands, music visuals, logo reveals and calm backgrounds. It is abstract, so it will not explain a step-by-step idea on its own.
keywords.prompt_example: "10-second logo reveal, generative particles animation, thousands of glowing particles flowing then gathering into the logo"

keywords.name: Gentle Giant
keywords.definition: A huge, strong character who turns out to be soft-hearted and kind. Big hands, careful movements, and often a tiny friend nearby.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for heartwarming scenes that play big against small. It works for people, creatures and animals alike.
keywords.prompt_example: "gentle giant troll holding a baby bird, misty forest"

keywords.name: Gentle Smile
keywords.definition: A soft, closed-lip or barely open smile. Calm and kind, rather than a big toothy grin.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when a big grin feels fake or too much. Lovely for portraits, book covers and quiet moments.
keywords.prompt_example: "older man with a gentle smile, holding a teacup, warm light"

keywords.name: Geometric Web Design
keywords.definition: A tidy site built from precise circles, triangles and rectangles, with neutral colors and clean Inter type that stays out of the way.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for architects, design studios, tech and finance brands that want order. Can feel cold without a warm accent color.
keywords.prompt_example: "website for an architecture studio, geometric web design, circles and triangles, sand and charcoal"

keywords.name: Gingham
keywords.definition: An even checkered pattern made by crossing stripes of one color with white. Think picnic blankets and summer dresses.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for sweet, homey, countryside feels. It reads as cute and simple, so it is not the choice for edgy or luxury moods.
keywords.prompt_example: "picnic basket on a red gingham blanket, summer meadow"

keywords.name: Glass Product 3D
keywords.definition: A see-through glass object floating in an endless black studio, outlined only by long strip lights that leave rainbow edges. You can see its insides, light pulses run through it on the beat, and it slowly comes apart, then snaps shut on the drop.
keywords.when_to_use: Great for sleek tech teasers, launch trailers and music-synced reveals. It looks premium but cold, so it is not for cozy or handmade brands.
keywords.prompt_example: "12-second tech teaser, glass product 3d animation, clear glass device floating in black, strip light reflections, parts drifting apart then snapping shut"

keywords.name: Glassmorphism UI
keywords.definition: Cards and panels that look like frosted glass: see-through, softly blurred, with thin glowing edges floating over colorful backgrounds.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for app screens, music players, weather apps and modern landing pages. Text on glass can be hard to read, so keep enough contrast.
keywords.prompt_example: "weather app screen, glassmorphism ui, frosted glass cards over a sunset gradient"

keywords.name: Glide
keywords.definition: A slow, weightless drift past the subject, as if carried on a breeze.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for dreamy, hypnotic, music-video moods.
keywords.prompt_example: "slow weightless glide past her through the flower field"

keywords.name: Glitch Datamosh
keywords.definition: A clean picture that breaks on the beat: color channels split apart, slices of the frame tear sideways and pixels smear, then everything snaps back to perfect until the next hit.
keywords.when_to_use: Great for music videos, tech launches and edgy reels that cut to a beat. Used all the time it becomes tiring, so save the glitches for the big moments.
keywords.prompt_example: "10-second music reel, glitch datamosh animation, clean frame tearing into rgb slices on every beat then snapping back"

keywords.name: Glitch Transition
keywords.definition: A burst of digital distortion covers the cut.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for tech, gaming and AI topics. Best added in the edit rather than prompted.
keywords.prompt_example: "add in the edit: a two-frame RGB glitch between the shots"

keywords.name: Glossy Glaze
keywords.definition: A shiny, mirror-like coating on food, like a donut glaze, a caramel layer or a sticky roast. It gleams with highlights.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when food needs to look rich, fresh and expensive. Too much shine can look plastic, so pair it with natural light.
keywords.prompt_example: "mirror glaze cake with glossy berry topping, soft window light"

keywords.name: Gold Leaf
keywords.definition: Paper-thin sheets of real gold pressed onto a surface, so parts of the art shine like metal. You see it in old religious icons, illuminated manuscripts and lacquerware.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for a precious, glowing accent on halos, borders or backgrounds. A little goes a long way; too much looks flat and brassy.
keywords.prompt_example: "heron among reeds, ink painting with gold leaf background"

keywords.name: Golden Age Comics
keywords.definition: The look of early comic books from the late 1930s to the early 1950s: simple bold heroes, flat bright colors, thick lines and slightly off-register printing on yellowed paper.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for retro heroes and charming vintage adventure. The simple style is part of the appeal, so do not expect modern realism.
keywords.prompt_example: "golden age comics cover, caped hero lifting a car, flat bright colors, yellowed paper"

keywords.name: Golden Autumn
keywords.definition: Peak fall: amber leaves, low warm sun, long shadows. Cozy and a little nostalgic.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for warmth, harvest scenes, and gentle melancholy.
keywords.prompt_example: "golden autumn park, falling leaves, long shadows"

keywords.name: Golden Hour
keywords.definition: The warm, honey-colored light you get just after sunrise or before sunset. It makes everything look softer, kinder, and more expensive.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when you want instant warmth and beauty with one word. If a prompt feels flat, this is the first thing to try.
keywords.prompt_example: "portrait of a gardener, golden hour light"

keywords.name: Golden Hour Grade
keywords.definition: Warm amber light of the sun's first and last hour, honeyed and forgiving.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for romance, nostalgia, and endings that feel earned.
keywords.prompt_example: "golden hour grade, field at last light"

keywords.name: Gond Painting
keywords.definition: Central Indian tribal art: animals and trees filled with rhythmic dot-and-dash patterns.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for pattern-rich nature illustration honoring the Gond tradition.
keywords.prompt_example: "tree of life, gond painting style"

keywords.name: Googie
keywords.definition: Space age roadside style from 1950s America: boomerang roofs, starbursts, tilted glass and big neon signs on diners, motels and car washes.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for fun retro diners, motels and atomic age streets. It reads strongly American, so lean into it.
keywords.prompt_example: "Googie diner with a boomerang roof and neon sign, desert night"

keywords.name: Gordon Parks
keywords.definition: (1912-2006) American photographer, filmmaker and writer who captured Black American life and the civil rights era for Life magazine. Warm, dignified portraits in rich color and black and white.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for heartfelt mid-century portraits and everyday family scenes with real warmth. Keep the people at the center and treat them with respect.
keywords.prompt_example: "family on a porch in 1950s Alabama, warm color, in the style of Gordon Parks"

keywords.name: Goth Pastel
keywords.definition: A black, deadpan, totally still frame with one unimpressed line of text, then a sudden explosion of candy rainbow gradients, sparkles, hearts and glossy stickers, then instantly back to stillness as if nothing happened.
keywords.when_to_use: Perfect for funny reels, ironic ads and personal brands with a dry sense of humor. The joke only works with good timing, and it can feel random without a punchline.
keywords.prompt_example: "10-second comedy reel, goth pastel animation, still black frame with deadpan text, then a burst of rainbow stickers and sparkles"

keywords.name: -goth
keywords.definition: Add -goth to a word to give it a dark, romantic twist: pastel goth, whimsigoth, bubble goth. Black lace, moons and moody shadows, mixed with whatever comes in front.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to make a sweet or ordinary theme a little spooky and dramatic. The word in front sets the mood, so choose it with care.
keywords.prompt_example: "garden goth tea party, black roses, overcast light"

keywords.name: Gothic Americana
keywords.definition: American gothic dread: lonely farmhouses, crows on wires, faith and dust.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for rural-dark storytelling scenes and southern-gothic moods.
keywords.prompt_example: "farmhouse at dusk, gothic americana"

keywords.name: Gothic Kawaii
keywords.definition: Cute meets creepy: pastel bats, smiling ghosts, lace and skulls in candy colors. Wednesday Addams meets Lisa Frank.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for playful dark content, stickers, and brand imagery with bite.
keywords.prompt_example: "gothic kawaii ghost tea party, pastel and black lace"

keywords.name: Gothic Novel
keywords.definition: The mood of an old Gothic book: crumbling castles, candlelit corridors, storms at the window and a heroine holding a lantern in the dark.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for romantic, shivery scenes full of mystery and old stone. Pairs well with candlelight and fog for instant atmosphere.
keywords.prompt_example: "gothic novel scene, girl with a lantern on a castle staircase, storm outside"

keywords.name: Graceful Minimal Web Design
keywords.definition: A graceful, refined site with delicate thin type, a minimal palette and polished layouts that feel quietly sophisticated.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for designers, boutiques, galleries and premium services. The delicate type can get lost on busy photos or small screens.
keywords.prompt_example: "website for a perfume boutique, graceful minimal web design, thin type, soft white and taupe"

keywords.name: Gradient Web Design
keywords.definition: Smooth blends of color washing across backgrounds, buttons and shapes, with Montserrat and Space Grotesk type for a modern, playful sense of depth.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for apps, music, startups and social brands that want a fresh, glowing look. Too many gradients at once can look muddy.
keywords.prompt_example: "homepage for a meditation app, gradient web design, peach to violet background"

keywords.name: Graffiti Pop Art
keywords.definition: Lowbrow street-pop blend: playful characters, bold outlines, KAWS-adjacent attitude.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for urban-pop characters and gallery-street crossover pieces.
keywords.prompt_example: "character mural, graffiti pop art"

keywords.name: Graffito
keywords.definition: Scratched-surface mark-making: images incised into plaster, paint, or stone.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for raw wall-texture art and ancient-meets-street surfaces.
keywords.prompt_example: "figures scratched into plaster wall, graffito"

keywords.name: Green Digital Rain UI
keywords.definition: A dark-only, hacker-movie look with glowing green code-like text, monospace type (every letter the same width), hairline borders and dense screens like a trading terminal.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for coding tools, security products, tech events and mysterious game sites. Hard to read for long stretches and wrong for warm brands.
keywords.prompt_example: "login screen for a puzzle game, green digital rain ui, falling green characters on black"

keywords.name: Grizzled Detective
keywords.definition: A tired, weather-beaten investigator with stubble, a rumpled coat and a long memory. They've seen too much and keep going anyway.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for crime stories, rainy cities and late-night offices. Add a city and an era to keep it from looking like every other noir.
keywords.prompt_example: "grizzled detective under a streetlamp, rain, neon reflections"

keywords.name: Ground Level
keywords.definition: The lens sits right on the floor, looking along it.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for feet, things rolling past, or a creature's-eye view.
keywords.prompt_example: "ground-level shot as the skateboard rolls toward us"

keywords.name: Ground Slash
keywords.definition: The camera skims just above the ground beside the subject and snaps its aim hard, up and back down.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it for low, aggressive sport or skate footage. Two snaps is plenty; more and it turns to mush.
keywords.prompt_example: "the camera skims just above the ground beside a skater, with two hard snaps of the aim from feet to head and back"

keywords.name: Grunge
keywords.definition: Worn, layered, deliberately undone: flannel, ripped denim, faded film texture, a little grime.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to rough up a scene that feels too clean or add 90s attitude.
keywords.prompt_example: "street portrait, grunge aesthetic, 35mm film"

keywords.name: Gunmetal
keywords.definition: A dark blue-gray metal with a soft satin shine. Serious, sleek and a little moody.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for tech products, watches, sci-fi gear and modern interiors. It reads darker than chrome, so add a light to bring out the edges.
keywords.prompt_example: "gunmetal wristwatch on black slate, single soft side light"

keywords.name: Gustav Klimt
keywords.definition: (1862-1918) Austrian painter of dreamy portraits wrapped in gold leaf, swirling patterns and mosaics. Romantic, decorative and shining.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for luxurious portraits, lovers and gold patterned backgrounds. Ask for gold leaf to get his famous golden look.
keywords.prompt_example: "two lovers embracing in a gold mosaic robe, in the style of Gustav Klimt"

keywords.name: Haida Art
keywords.definition: Pacific Northwest Indigenous formline art: bold ovoids, split forms, powerful crest animals.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for striking formline animal designs in the Haida tradition.
keywords.prompt_example: "raven design, haida formline art"

keywords.name: Halftone Comic
keywords.definition: A vintage comic page come to life: thick black outlines, flat colors filled with printed dots, panels that wipe in one after another, and impact bursts that shake the frame.
keywords.when_to_use: Fun for punchy reels, product launches and story recaps with big moments. Busy pages can crowd out text, so keep each panel to one idea.
keywords.prompt_example: "12-second launch reel, halftone comic animation, panels wiping in, a starburst with a sound word shaking the frame"

keywords.name: Halston
keywords.definition: American designer Halston (1932-1990) defined 1970s glamour with simple, fluid pieces: jersey halter gowns, caftans, wrap shapes and clean minimal lines that moved on the dance floor.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for sleek 1970s nightlife and minimalist evening wear. Great with disco light, but keep the clothes simple to stay true to him.
keywords.prompt_example: "flowing red jersey halter gown in the style of halston, 1970s nightclub, mirror ball"

keywords.name: Hamburger Menu
keywords.definition: An icon of three stacked lines that opens a hidden menu when tapped. Here the lines morph into an X while the menu slides down, so you know how to close it.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it on small screens to tuck navigation away and keep the page clean. Hidden menus get used less, so keep your most important link visible too.
keywords.prompt_example: "Add a three-line menu icon to the header that morphs into an X when clicked and slides a full-width menu with Home, Library, Lessons and Contact down from the top."

keywords.name: Hammered Gold
keywords.definition: Gold covered in tiny dents and dimples from being shaped by hand. Each little dip catches the light and sparkles.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for luxury jewelry, rich tableware and opulent details. It looks warmer and more handmade than smooth gold.
keywords.prompt_example: "hammered gold bowl on black velvet, soft spotlight"

keywords.name: Hanbok
keywords.definition: Traditional Korean clothing. For women, a short jacket called a jeogori over a full, high-waisted skirt called a chima; for men, a jacket with roomy trousers. Soft colors and graceful lines.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for Korean family celebrations and portraits. Hanbok is worn for special days like Seollal, Chuseok, a baby's first birthday and weddings, so show it with that care.
keywords.prompt_example: "young woman in a pastel pink hanbok, palace courtyard in autumn"

keywords.name: Hand Over Lens
keywords.definition: Hands cover the lens, then open on a new scene.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for playful resets and reveals.
keywords.prompt_example: "she covers the lens with both hands; as they part she is somewhere new"

keywords.name: Handheld
keywords.definition: Unstabilized camera with natural shake and drift; human, urgent, imperfect.
