keywords.when_to_use: Use for documentary realism, panic, or intimacy that polish would flatten.
keywords.prompt_example: "handheld camera, kitchen argument, urgent energy"

keywords.name: Hard Cut
keywords.definition: The plain, everyday join: one shot simply ends and the next one begins.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it when nothing fancier earns its place, which is most of the time. It is added in editing, not in the prompt: make two clips and join them.
keywords.prompt_example: "in the edit, place clip B straight after clip A, with the runner moving left to right in both"

keywords.name: Hard Edge Painting
keywords.definition: Crisp geometric color fields with razor-clean boundaries; no brushwork, no blending.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for bold graphic compositions and modernist poster energy.
keywords.prompt_example: "abstract composition, hard edge painting"

keywords.name: Hard Light
keywords.definition: Small, direct sources casting crisp shadows and sharp texture; unforgiving and graphic.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for noir edges, desert sun, and faces with history.
keywords.prompt_example: "hard light across his face, blinds striping shadow"

keywords.name: Harlem Renaissance
keywords.definition: 1920s Black American artistic flowering: jazz-age portraiture, bold dignity, rhythmic composition.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for celebratory historical portraits and jazz-era scenes.
keywords.prompt_example: "jazz club scene, harlem renaissance painting"

keywords.name: Harry Clarke
keywords.definition: (1889-1931) Irish stained glass artist and illustrator of eerie fairy tales and Edgar Allan Poe stories. Super fine ink detail, jewel patterns and pale, haunting faces.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for dark, ornate, spooky illustrations full of tiny detail. Great for gothic stories, less so for cheerful ones.
keywords.prompt_example: "pale queen in a jewel-patterned gown, ink illustration, in the style of Harry Clarke"

keywords.name: Head Dip Match Cut
keywords.definition: The subject dips their head in one place and lifts it in another.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it for portrait films, or to show a whole life in a few cuts. Keep the framing and size the same in both places.
keywords.prompt_example: "an old fisherman bows his head on a misty pier; as he lifts it he is in a busy city cafe, same framing and size"

keywords.name: Heat Haze
keywords.definition: The shimmery, wavy air above hot roads and deserts. You can feel the temperature.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for deserts, summer roads, and tension. It adds motion to still scenes.
keywords.prompt_example: "empty desert highway, heat haze on the horizon"

keywords.name: Henri Cartier-Bresson
keywords.definition: (1908-2004) French photographer who mastered the decisive moment, the split second when everything in a street scene lines up just right. Black and white, natural and beautifully balanced.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for candid street scenes with perfect timing and shape. Works best with simple everyday action, like someone jumping a puddle.
keywords.prompt_example: "man leaping over a puddle in a Paris street, in the style of Henri Cartier-Bresson"

keywords.name: Henri Matisse
keywords.definition: (1869-1954) French painter who, late in life, made bright paper cut-outs: shapes snipped from hand-painted paper, seaweed forms, stars and dancers in pure, joyful color.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for bold, cheerful compositions with simple shapes, posters and anything that should feel like a celebration.
keywords.prompt_example: "swimmers among seaweed shapes, in the style of Henri Matisse paper cut-outs"

keywords.name: Herringbone
keywords.definition: Rows of short slanted lines that flip direction, like the bones of a fish. Found in tweed fabric and parquet wood floors.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for cozy tailoring, wooden floors and tiled walls. From far away it can look like plain texture, so get closer if you want it seen.
keywords.prompt_example: "herringbone oak floor in a sunny reading nook"

keywords.name: Hidden Image
keywords.definition: A picture with a second picture tucked inside it, like a forest whose trees form a face when you step back.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for puzzles, posters and magical double meanings. It is tricky for AI, so name both images clearly and keep the scene simple.
keywords.prompt_example: "autumn forest where the trees form a hidden image of an owl"

keywords.name: Hieronymus Bosch
keywords.definition: (c. 1450-1516) Dutch painter of crowded, strange dream worlds full of tiny creatures, odd machines and giant fruit. Funny, spooky and endlessly weird.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for surreal, busy fantasy landscapes packed with little details. Expect chaos, so it is not for simple, clean images.
keywords.prompt_example: "crowded fantasy garden with tiny strange creatures and giant strawberries, in the style of Hieronymus Bosch"

keywords.name: High Angle
keywords.definition: Camera looks down, diminishing the subject or mapping the scene.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for vulnerability, surveillance moods, or clear spatial layouts.
keywords.prompt_example: "high angle on the child lost in the crowd"

keywords.name: High Fashion
keywords.definition: Editorial runway polish: dramatic styling, sculptural garments, magazine-cover confidence.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for fashion editorials and portraits that should look expensive.
keywords.prompt_example: "editorial portrait, high fashion, avant-garde gown"

keywords.name: High-Key Lighting
keywords.definition: Bright, even, nearly shadowless illumination; open and optimistic.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for comedy, commercials, and worlds without secrets.
keywords.prompt_example: "morning kitchen scene, high-key lighting"

keywords.name: High Selfie Angle
keywords.definition: The classic selfie view, with the camera held above the head and tilted down. Big eyes, small chin and an arm reaching just out of frame.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for casual phone-style portraits and social media looks. Models may add a stretched arm or a phone, so say no phone visible if you want it hidden.
keywords.prompt_example: "high selfie angle of a smiling girl at a summer festival, phone photo"

keywords.name: Highland Cow
keywords.definition: A shaggy Scottish cow with long ginger hair over its eyes and wide curved horns. Scruffy, gentle and wildly lovable.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for cozy countryside scenes, cute farm portraits and misty hills. The fringe over the eyes is the charm, so keep the face close.
keywords.prompt_example: "highland cow in misty Scottish hills, fog, overcast light"

keywords.name: Hilma af Klint
keywords.definition: (1862-1944) Swedish painter who made huge, colorful abstract paintings years before abstract art was famous. Spirals, circles, petals and soft pastel symbols.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for spiritual, cosmic and geometric abstract art with gentle color. Not for realistic scenes.
keywords.prompt_example: "large abstract painting of spirals and petals, pastel pink and blue, in the style of Hilma af Klint"

keywords.name: Hokusai
keywords.definition: (c. 1760-1849) Japanese artist behind The Great Wave, known for woodblock prints with flat bold colors, crisp outlines, deep blues and views of Mount Fuji.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for Japanese print-style waves, mountains and everyday scenes. It is a flat print look, so skip it for realism.
keywords.prompt_example: "giant wave crashing near a lighthouse, woodblock print, in the style of Hokusai"

keywords.name: Hollywood Regency
keywords.definition: Old Hollywood glamour at home: glossy lacquer, mirrored furniture, gold accents, bold black and white, and jewel-colored velvet.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for glamorous, a little theatrical rooms with movie star energy. Too much gold can look cheap, so balance it with black or white.
keywords.prompt_example: "Hollywood Regency dressing room, mirrored vanity, emerald velvet, gold lamps"

keywords.name: Hologram HUD
keywords.definition: A gadget is scanned into a glowing wireframe above a round projector. A target box snaps onto one part, its shell slides open, a line pulls out and scrambled symbols roll into the real number.
keywords.when_to_use: Great for tech product reveals, sci-fi trailers and spec breakdowns. It needs a real object with parts worth pointing at, and too many labels quickly crowd the frame.
keywords.prompt_example: "12-second tech reveal, hologram hud animation, glowing blue wireframe watch above a projector, target box snapping onto a part"

keywords.name: Holographic Shimmer
keywords.definition: A rainbow sheen that shifts across a surface, like a hologram sticker or a soap bubble. Colors slide from pink to blue to gold as the light moves.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for futuristic fashion, packaging, stickers and dreamy objects. It's a bit loud, so put it on one thing rather than the whole scene.
keywords.prompt_example: "holographic shimmer jacket, white studio, soft light"

keywords.name: Homecoming
keywords.definition: A traveler arriving back where they started, changed by the journey. Porch lights on, a dog running out, a familiar door seen with new eyes.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for warm, emotional endings and reunions. Golden light and a slightly wider shot help it feel like the end of a long story.
keywords.prompt_example: "homecoming, tired sailor walking up a lantern-lit path to a cottage, dog running out"

keywords.name: Hopi Art
keywords.definition: Hopi visual tradition: kachina imagery, pottery motifs, desert palettes with deep symbolism.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for respectful Southwest-rooted pattern and pottery scenes.
keywords.prompt_example: "pottery motifs, hopi art tradition"

keywords.name: Horizontal Scroll
keywords.definition: Scrolling down the page moves a row of big cards sideways across the screen instead. It turns a normal scroll into a sideways gallery or timeline.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it for a timeline, a set of chapters or a portfolio row that deserves a moment of attention. It can confuse people on phones, so test it there and keep a simple fallback.
keywords.prompt_example: "When I scroll down, move this row of large cards sideways across the screen like a timeline"

keywords.name: Houndstooth
keywords.definition: A broken check made of little jagged four-pointed shapes, usually black and white. Classic, sharp and a little bit British tailoring.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for fashion, coats and smart retro looks. Large areas of it can shimmer or warp, so keep it on clothing or trim.
keywords.prompt_example: "woman in a houndstooth coat on a rainy street"

keywords.name: Hover Lift
keywords.definition: When the mouse passes over a card, it rises a little and casts a deeper shadow, then settles back down when the mouse leaves. It tells you the card can be clicked.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it on grids of clickable cards, like products, trips or articles. Phones have no hover, so make sure the cards still look tappable without it.
keywords.prompt_example: "Make each card lift up with a deeper shadow when I hover over it, and settle back when I move away"

keywords.name: Huipil
keywords.definition: A loose tunic made from rectangles of handwoven cloth, worn by Indigenous women in southern Mexico and Guatemala. Covered in woven and embroidered flowers, birds and geometric bands.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for portraits and market scenes with real cultural detail. Designs often tell which town or community the weaver comes from, and some huipiles are made only for ceremonies.
keywords.prompt_example: "woman weaving on a backstrap loom, wearing an embroidered huipil, guatemalan highlands"

keywords.name: Hyper Motion Product
keywords.definition: A high-speed close-up commercial where flames lick, splashes freeze mid-air and crumbs hang in slow motion, then everything snaps to full speed on the beat and the product lands center frame with its name slammed on top.
keywords.when_to_use: Made for food, drink and product ads that need to feel exciting. It depends on great close-up footage or renders, and it is overkill for quiet or talky content.
keywords.prompt_example: "8-second snack ad, hyper motion product shot, crumbs hanging in slow motion then snapping to full speed as the bag lands"

keywords.name: Hyperspace Noir
keywords.definition: Detective-story shadow in deep space: neon-lit starships, trench coats among the stars.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for sci-fi mystery scenes with hardboiled mood.
keywords.prompt_example: "detective on a space station, hyperspace noir"

keywords.name: Iconography
keywords.definition: Symbol-dense sacred-art styling: gold leaf, flat perspective, figures loaded with meaning.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for reverent stylized portraits and symbolic compositions.
keywords.prompt_example: "portrait in byzantine iconography style, gold leaf"

keywords.name: Ikat
keywords.definition: A woven pattern with soft, feathery edges, because the threads are dyed in sections before weaving. It is a centuries-old craft from places like Indonesia, Central Asia and India.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for warm, handmade textiles with a blurred, dreamy edge. AI often makes it too sharp, so ask for blurred edges and woven texture.
keywords.prompt_example: "indigo ikat cushion on a rattan chair, blurred feathered edges"

keywords.name: Illuminated Manuscript
keywords.definition: A handwritten page from the Middle Ages, glowing with gold leaf, rich colors and a giant decorated first letter. Vines, tiny animals and little figures crawl around the margins.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for fantasy, history and anything that should feel sacred or precious. The writing will usually be pretend script, so treat it as decoration.
keywords.prompt_example: "illuminated manuscript page of a fox reading a book, gold leaf border"

keywords.name: Illustration
keywords.definition: General illustrated rendering: visible artistic interpretation rather than photographic realism.
keywords.when_to_use: Use as a base style word when you want drawn, not photographed.
keywords.prompt_example: "cottage by a river, illustration"

keywords.name: Image Carousel
keywords.definition: A row of big pictures that slides along one at a time, with dots underneath showing which one you are on. Arrows on the sides move it forward or back.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it to show a few featured pictures in the space of one. Many people never look past the first slide, so put the best one first.
keywords.prompt_example: "Build an image carousel with four large slides that glide one step at a time, arrow buttons on each side and dots below that show the current slide"

keywords.name: Image Zoom on Hover
keywords.definition: When the mouse rests on a picture, the image slowly zooms in inside its frame while a caption slides up from the bottom. The frame stays the same size; only the picture grows.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it on galleries, portfolios and shop items to invite a closer look. Keep the zoom slow and small, or it feels jumpy.
keywords.prompt_example: "When I hover a photo card, slowly zoom the image inside its frame and slide a caption up from the bottom"

keywords.name: Immersive Exhibit Web Design
keywords.definition: A site that feels like walking through an interactive museum exhibit, all on one continuous deep green canvas with crisp white type, storytelling, animation and little game-like moments.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for campaigns, museums, brand stories and product launches people explore once. Slow for visitors who just want quick facts.
keywords.prompt_example: "rainforest museum website, immersive exhibit web design, deep green canvas, scroll story with mini games"

keywords.name: Impasto
keywords.definition: Paint laid on so thickly that it stands up off the canvas in ridges and peaks. You can almost feel every brushstroke.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when you want rich, touchable texture and energy. All that surface can fight with fine detail, so keep the subject simple.
keywords.prompt_example: "sunflowers in a clay jug, impasto oil painting"

keywords.name: Impasto Oil Animation
keywords.definition: A moving oil painting laid on with a palette knife: big, flat, sharp-edged planes of thick paint, lit from the side so every ridge shows. Only what the story moves moves, like rain, a figure or the light.
keywords.when_to_use: Great for emotional stories, music videos and artful brand films. Thick paint hides small details, so keep scenes simple and bold.
keywords.prompt_example: "15-second story clip, impasto oil animation, thick palette knife paint, a figure opening an umbrella as rain moves across"

keywords.name: Impossible Staircase
keywords.definition: Stairs that seem to climb forever in a loop, always going up yet ending where they started.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for puzzling, dreamlike architecture. AI often makes ordinary stairs, so add 'endless looping stairs' and a high angle.
keywords.prompt_example: "impossible staircase looping around a stone tower, high angle"

keywords.name: Impossible Triangle
keywords.definition: A solid-looking triangle whose three beams join in a way that could never exist in real space.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for logos, sculptures and puzzling architecture. AI often fixes it into a normal triangle, so add 'optical illusion' to the prompt.
keywords.prompt_example: "impossible triangle sculpture in a desert, optical illusion"

keywords.name: Industrial Loft
keywords.definition: Old factory space turned home: exposed brick, steel beams, giant windows, concrete floors and pipes left showing.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for creative city apartments, studios and moody urban scenes. Can feel cold, so add warm lamps or leather.
keywords.prompt_example: "industrial loft apartment, exposed brick, tall steel windows, evening"

keywords.name: Infinite Marquee
keywords.definition: Rows of big words or little labels glide sideways forever in a smooth endless loop, often with rows moving in opposite directions.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it for a band of keywords, partner badges or short claims that adds energy to a page. Do not put important information in it, since moving text is hard to read.
keywords.prompt_example: "Add an infinite marquee section: two rows of big words sliding sideways in opposite directions, looping seamlessly with faded edges."

keywords.name: Infinite Scroll
keywords.definition: As you scroll to the bottom of a feed, a small loading sign appears and more items arrive below, so the list never seems to end.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it for photo feeds, galleries and social style lists that people browse casually. Avoid it when people need to reach a footer or find their place again.
keywords.prompt_example: "Make my gallery load more cards when I scroll to the bottom, with a small spinner while the new ones arrive."

keywords.name: Infinity Mirror
keywords.definition: Two mirrors facing each other, making lights or reflections repeat in a tunnel that seems to go on forever.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for glowing art rooms, dreamy portraits and sci-fi halls. It loves points of light, so add lanterns, LEDs or neon.
keywords.prompt_example: "infinity mirror room filled with tiny pink lights"

keywords.name: Infinity Polka Dots
keywords.definition: Dots everywhere: bold polka dots covering walls, floors, objects and people until everything melts into one endless pattern, often red and white or yellow and black.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for immersive, playful installation scenes, statement fashion and dreamy rooms that feel like they go on forever.
keywords.prompt_example: "room covered in red polka dots with mirrored walls, infinity polka dots"

keywords.name: Infographic
keywords.definition: A clean, friendly layout that explains something with icons, simple charts, arrows and short labels. It looks like a poster you would pin up in a classroom.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when you want to explain a process or show facts at a glance. Keep the words few and short, because AI text can still come out scrambled.
keywords.prompt_example: "infographic about how bees make honey, flat icons, warm yellow palette"

keywords.name: Infrared Film
keywords.definition: Film that sees invisible light, turning green leaves and grass bright white or candy pink while skies go dark. Familiar places suddenly look like another planet.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for surreal landscapes and dreamy, otherworldly nature. Say black and white infrared for white trees, or color infrared for pink trees.
keywords.prompt_example: "color infrared photo of a forest lake, pink trees"

keywords.name: Ink and Watercolor
keywords.definition: Crisp pen lines with soft watercolor washes under them. The lines hold the shape, the paint adds mood.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when plain watercolor gets too blurry and you want clear detail. Great for travel sketches, botanicals and storybook scenes.
keywords.prompt_example: "ink and watercolor sketch of a corner cafe in the rain"

keywords.name: Ink in Water
keywords.definition: Clouds of ink blooming and curling slowly through clear water. Soft, swirling shapes that feel alive.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for abstract backgrounds, title cards and calm, hypnotic video. It's a mood rather than a subject, so add color words.
keywords.prompt_example: "purple and gold ink in water, slow swirl, black background"

keywords.name: Ink Wash Animation
keywords.definition: A quiet East Asian ink painting that paints itself: one brush lays tapering strokes, grey washes bloom outward like ink in water, and mountains or birds rise out of mist. Most of the frame stays empty paper and the camera drifts slowly.
keywords.when_to_use: Beautiful for calm, reflective openers, poetry, tea or wellness brands. It is meant to be slow and spare, so it will not carry a busy, info-heavy video.
keywords.prompt_example: "12-second calm opener, ink wash animation, a mountain rising from mist as grey ink blooms across rice paper"

keywords.name: Insert Shot
keywords.definition: A quick cut to one small detail: a text message, a ring, a button.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to hand the viewer one important piece of information fast.
keywords.prompt_example: "insert shot of her phone lighting up with a message"

keywords.name: Intentional Camera Movement
keywords.definition: Moving the camera on purpose while the photo is taken, so trees, lights or the sea smear into painterly streaks.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for abstract, painterly nature and city images. Nothing will be sharp, and that is the point.
keywords.prompt_example: "intentional camera movement photo of a birch forest, vertical streaks"

keywords.name: Iridescent
keywords.definition: A surface that shifts colors as it catches light, like soap bubbles, beetle shells, or oil on water.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for magic, luxury, and dreamlike surfaces. A little goes a long way.
keywords.prompt_example: "iridescent silk gown, studio light"

keywords.name: Irving Penn
keywords.definition: (1917-2009) American photographer known for elegant fashion portraits and still lifes against plain gray backdrops. Calm, precise and beautifully lit, like a museum piece.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for clean studio portraits, fashion and simple, perfect still lifes. It is a studio look, so it will not help outdoor scenes.
keywords.prompt_example: "still life of ripe pears on a gray backdrop, in the style of Irving Penn"

keywords.name: Islamic Geometric Pattern
keywords.definition: Interlocking stars, polygons and rosettes that repeat endlessly, found in tilework, carved wood and plaster across the Islamic world. Precise, balanced and mesmerizing.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for tiles, ceilings, doorways and decorative backgrounds. AI can get the geometry slightly off, so expect to pick the cleanest result.
keywords.prompt_example: "courtyard ceiling with Islamic geometric pattern, turquoise and gold tiles"

keywords.name: Isometric Illustration
keywords.definition: A tidy, angled view where everything is seen from above at the same slant, with nothing shrinking into the distance. Like a tiny diorama or a game map.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for cute room cutaways, maps and miniature worlds. It doesn't do dramatic perspective, so leave camera angle words out.
keywords.prompt_example: "isometric illustration of a cozy bookshop interior, soft colors"

keywords.name: Isometric Infographic Animation
keywords.definition: A system diagram come alive: one floating board of flat three-tone blocks seen from an angle, a dashed route leading from station to station, things slicing open to show their insides, and numbers shown as rows of tiny icons.
keywords.when_to_use: Ideal for explaining how a system, process or business works. It takes planning to lay out the board, so it is too much for a quick one-fact post.
keywords.prompt_example: "30-second process explainer, isometric infographic animation, dashed route drawing between flat blocks, a factory slicing open to show inside"

keywords.name: Isometric Render
keywords.definition: A tidy 3D view from above at an angle, with no vanishing point, so it looks like a little game board or dollhouse.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for cozy rooms, tiny towns and explainer art. The camera angle is fixed, so it is not for dramatic or cinematic shots.
keywords.prompt_example: "isometric render of a tiny bakery, warm morning light"

keywords.name: Ivan Bilibin
keywords.definition: (1876-1942) Russian illustrator of folk tales, with bold outlines, flat bright colors and fancy patterned borders inspired by old Russian art.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for Slavic fairy tales, firebirds and decorated storybook pages. Ask for an ornamental border to get the full page look.
keywords.prompt_example: "firebird in a dark forest with ornamental border, in the style of Ivan Bilibin"

keywords.name: J-Cut
keywords.definition: The next scene's sound arrives before its picture; audio leads the way in.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for smooth scene flow and anticipation.
keywords.prompt_example: "J-cut: the crowd noise rises before we see the stadium"

keywords.name: Jan van Eyck
keywords.definition: (c. 1390-1441) Early Flemish painter famous for jewel-bright oil colors and unbelievable detail, down to every bead, fur trim and tiny mirror reflection.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for richly detailed portraits and rooms that feel frozen in time. Great with fabrics, jewels and fine textures.
keywords.prompt_example: "merchant couple in a candlelit room with a round mirror, in the style of Jan van Eyck"

keywords.name: Japandi
keywords.definition: A calm mix of Japanese and Scandinavian rooms: low wood furniture, linen, paper lamps, soft beige and gray, and almost no clutter.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for peaceful, airy rooms that feel like a deep breath. If you want color or personality, this is the wrong word.
keywords.prompt_example: "reading nook, Japandi interior, morning light"

keywords.name: Jazz Club
keywords.definition: A dim, smoky room with a small stage, a glowing saxophone, round tables and warm lamps. Late-night and full of soul.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for moody night scenes, vintage glamour and cozy after-hours stories. It loves warm light and deep shadows.
keywords.prompt_example: "jazz club stage, saxophone player in a spotlight, smoky air, warm lamps"

keywords.name: Jean-Michel Frank
keywords.definition: French designer (1895-1941) who made quiet luxury: plain rooms in cream and beige, walls of parchment or straw, and chunky simple chairs and tables.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for soft, minimal, very rich-looking rooms. The magic is in the textures, so name materials like parchment, straw or leather.
keywords.prompt_example: "cream salon with parchment walls and block armchairs, Jean-Michel Frank style"

keywords.name: Jellyfish
keywords.definition: Soft, see-through bells trailing long ribbon tentacles, drifting like living lanterns. In the dark they can glow.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for calm underwater scenes, dreamy floating shapes and glowing night images. Lovely in video because they move so slowly.
keywords.prompt_example: "jellyfish drifting in dark water, bioluminescence, ethereal"

keywords.name: Jewel Tones
keywords.definition: Deep, saturated colors named after gems: emerald, ruby, sapphire, amethyst. Rich and confident.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for luxury, drama, and depth. They love dark backgrounds and velvet textures.
keywords.prompt_example: "portrait in jewel tones, emerald background"

keywords.name: Jib Reveal
keywords.definition: The camera swoops down from above in one arc, glides along the subject and lands on a detail.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it for product or character intros that finish on one feature. Name the exact detail to land on, or it may stop somewhere random.
keywords.prompt_example: "jib down from above in one arc, glide along a vintage motorbike and settle close on its chrome headlamp"

keywords.name: J.M.W. Turner
keywords.definition: (1775-1851) English painter of stormy seas, blazing sunsets and ships lost in golden mist. Light and weather swallow everything.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for epic, hazy, glowing skies and wild weather. Shapes dissolve, so do not expect crisp detail.
keywords.prompt_example: "ship in a storm at sunset, golden mist, in the style of J.M.W. Turner"

keywords.name: Johannes Vermeer
keywords.definition: (1632-1675) Dutch painter of quiet indoor scenes, often a woman by a window in soft daylight. Pearly light, cool blues and yellows, and calm stillness.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for peaceful, softly lit interiors and portraits. Add window light from the left to get his signature look.
keywords.prompt_example: "woman pouring milk by a window, in the style of Johannes Vermeer"

keywords.name: John Tenniel
keywords.definition: (1820-1914) English illustrator who drew the first pictures for Alice's Adventures in Wonderland. Crisp black and white engraved lines and odd, slightly stiff characters.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for Victorian storybook scenes and curious, Alice-like characters. It is black and white line work, so add color only if you really want it.
keywords.prompt_example: "rabbit in a waistcoat checking a pocket watch, in the style of John Tenniel"

keywords.name: Jump Cut
keywords.definition: The camera stays put while time jumps between cuts, so things pop in, out or around.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for routines, comedy and fast montages.
keywords.prompt_example: "jump cuts on a locked frame as more friends appear beside her"

keywords.name: Kaiju Film
keywords.definition: The classic Japanese giant monster movie: a towering creature stomping through a miniature city, tiny tanks and planes, smoke, sparks and screaming crowds.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for big, playful destruction and a sense of huge scale. Add 'miniature set' if you want the handmade, person-in-a-suit charm of the old films.
keywords.prompt_example: "kaiju film still, giant lizard monster wading through a toy-like harbor city at night"

keywords.name: Kangra Painting
keywords.definition: Himalayan miniature school: lyrical romance scenes, delicate faces, lush green landscapes.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for tender miniature-style narrative scenes.
keywords.prompt_example: "lovers in a garden, kangra miniature painting"

keywords.name: Karesansui
keywords.definition: Japanese dry rock garden aesthetic: raked gravel, placed stones, emptiness as design.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for meditative minimal scenes and zen-garden compositions.
keywords.prompt_example: "karesansui rock garden, raked gravel, dawn"

keywords.name: Kawaii Gamer
keywords.definition: Cute-culture meets gaming setup: pastel peripherals, plushies, RGB glow softened into candy colors.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for cozy tech scenes, streamer aesthetics, or anything that should feel playful and plugged-in.
keywords.prompt_example: "desk setup, kawaii gamer aesthetic, pastel pink"

keywords.name: -kei
keywords.definition: Kei is Japanese for 'style' or 'type,' used in street fashion names like mori kei and dolly kei. Adding it suggests a full Japanese street-style outfit built around one idea.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for fashion portraits and character outfits. It's about clothing and styling, so it does little for landscapes.
keywords.prompt_example: "teatime kei outfit, lace and pastel layers, street portrait"

keywords.name: Kente Cloth
keywords.definition: Brightly colored cloth from Ghana, made by the Asante and Ewe peoples by weaving narrow strips on a loom and sewing them together. Bold blocks of gold, green, red and black, each pattern with its own name and meaning.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for celebrations, portraits and graduation scenes. Kente was once reserved for royalty and is still worn for important ceremonies, so treat it as a meaningful cloth, not a random pattern.
keywords.prompt_example: "graduate wearing a kente cloth stole, proud smile, sunny campus lawn"

keywords.name: Keynote Reveal
keywords.definition: Product-launch presentation style: one idea per screen, a soft glowing background, frosted-glass cards and big numbers that land the moment they're mentioned.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for software tutorials, feature announcements and showing off a product or a result.
keywords.prompt_example: "giant number 8 fades up on a dark navy background, frosted glass card, product keynote style"

keywords.name: Kimono
keywords.definition: Japan's traditional robe: a straight, T-shaped garment wrapped around the body and tied with a wide sash called an obi. Fabrics range from simple cotton to silk painted with flowers and cranes.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for Japanese gardens, tea ceremonies and festivals. Kimono wrap left side over right; right over left is reserved for dressing the deceased, so check your results.
keywords.prompt_example: "woman in a silk kimono with crane pattern, kyoto garden, morning light"

keywords.name: Kinetic Art
keywords.definition: Art built around real or implied movement: spinning, swaying, optically vibrating forms.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for compositions that need motion energy in a still frame.
keywords.prompt_example: "kinetic sculpture in a plaza, sense of motion"

keywords.name: Kinetic Type Animation
keywords.definition: Words are the whole show: each spoken word lands on screen right as it is said, slamming, popping, sliding and stacking into bold layouts. When a block is full it pushes back and the next one slams in front.
keywords.when_to_use: Great for quotes, voiceover reels, lyric videos and hooks. It needs a clear, well-timed voice track, and long sentences get hard to read.
keywords.prompt_example: "15-second quote reel, kinetic type animation, bold words slamming in on each spoken word and stacking into blocks"

keywords.name: Kinetic Typography
keywords.definition: Words are the actors: the key word slams onto the screen on the beat, supporting words slide up from below, and there's only ever one thing to read at a time.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for openers, quotes, lists and short-form video where the words carry the message.
keywords.prompt_example: "the word AGENTS slams onto a black screen in bold yellow, kinetic typography"

keywords.name: Kintsugi
keywords.definition: The Japanese art of mending broken pottery with gold, so the cracks become shining golden rivers across the piece.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for healing, beauty in flaws and quiet luxury. Works as a metaphor too, like gold seams on a face or a heart.
keywords.prompt_example: "black kintsugi bowl with gold seams, dark slate, single soft light"

keywords.name: Kishangarh Painting
keywords.definition: Rajasthani miniature style famed for elongated eyes and elegant, lotus-like profiles.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for graceful miniature portraits in the Bani Thani tradition.
keywords.prompt_example: "portrait in kishangarh miniature style"

keywords.name: Knitting
keywords.definition: Soft loops of yarn growing off two needles, often with a ball of wool rolling nearby. Chunky stitches read as warmth you can almost feel.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for cozy winter scenes, slow-living moments, or a gentle hands-at-work shot. Close crops work best, since fine stitches can turn to mush in wide shots.
keywords.prompt_example: "knitting a chunky cream scarf by the window, rainy afternoon"

keywords.name: Knolling
keywords.definition: Objects laid out flat and lined up at neat right angles, every item in its own space. Very tidy and very satisfying.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for tool kits, gear layouts and 'what's in my bag' images. AI can repeat or merge items, so keep the object list short.
keywords.prompt_example: "knolling of vintage camera gear on kraft paper, top-down"

keywords.name: Kodachrome
keywords.definition: A famous old color slide film with rich reds, deep blues and warm, glowing skin. Think 1950s and 60s holiday slides.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for vivid, warm, mid-century color that feels real but extra beautiful. It pushes color hard, so keep the scene simple.
keywords.prompt_example: "Kodachrome photo of a 1960s roadside diner at noon"

keywords.name: Koi
keywords.definition: Big ornamental carp in white, orange, red and black, gliding through clear pond water. Calm, lucky and very Japanese garden.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for peaceful pond scenes and swirling patterns of fish. They look best seen from above through clear water.
keywords.prompt_example: "koi swimming in a clear pond under floating maple leaves, top-down view"

keywords.name: L-Cut
keywords.definition: The previous scene's audio lingers over the new image; sound refuses to leave.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for reactions carrying into consequences and conversational flow.
keywords.prompt_example: "L-cut: her words continue over his face at the window"

keywords.name: Lab Notebook
keywords.definition: A scientist's working notebook: grid paper filled with handwritten notes, quick sketches, taped-in photos, coffee rings and crossed-out numbers.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for science stories, research moods and backgrounds with a hands-on feel. Handwriting will be decorative, not readable.
keywords.prompt_example: "open lab notebook on a bench, handwritten notes and sketches of molecules, glass beakers nearby"

keywords.name: Land Art
keywords.definition: Earth itself as medium: spirals of stone, lines in desert, art at landscape scale.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for monumental outdoor interventions and aerial-view earthworks.
keywords.prompt_example: "stone spiral in a salt flat, land art, aerial view"

keywords.name: Laugh Lines
keywords.definition: The soft creases around the eyes and mouth that come from years of smiling. They make a face look kind and lived-in.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for honest, warm portraits of adults, especially older people. AI tends to smooth skin, so this word helps keep real character.
keywords.prompt_example: "close-up of a fisherman with laugh lines, overcast light"

keywords.name: Lavender
keywords.definition: A pale, soft purple, like the flowers of the lavender plant. Gentle, dreamy and a little bit magical.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for calm, sweet and fairy tale moods. It can wash out in bright light, so add a deeper purple if the image feels faded.
keywords.prompt_example: "lavender field at dusk, soft haze"

keywords.name: Layered Surfaces UI
keywords.definition: A tidy app look built from flat sheets stacked in layers, each with a soft shadow, plus colors that follow one theme and small smooth motions when you tap.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for phone apps, dashboards and tools that need to work well on every screen size. Common enough that it can feel familiar rather than special.
keywords.prompt_example: "recipe app screens, layered surfaces ui, stacked cards with soft shadows, round action button"

keywords.name: Layered Trifle
keywords.definition: A tall glass bowl showing neat stripes of sponge cake, custard, fruit and whipped cream. Pretty from the side, like a dessert cross-section.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for celebration tables and vintage-style dessert shots. Shoot from the side so the layers show.
keywords.prompt_example: "layered trifle with raspberries and cream in a glass bowl, side view"

keywords.name: Le Corbusier
keywords.definition: Swiss-French architect (1887-1965) who made clean white boxes lifted on slim pillars, with long strip windows and flat roof gardens. Later work used chunky raw concrete.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for crisp early modern homes and bold concrete housing blocks. Can look cold, so warm it up with sunlight or plants.
keywords.prompt_example: "white villa raised on thin pillars, Le Corbusier style, summer lawn"

keywords.name: Leading Lines
keywords.definition: Lines in the scene, like roads, rails or fences, that run toward your subject.
keywords.when_to_use: Use them to pull the eye straight to what matters. Name the lines in your prompt so the model knows what to build.
keywords.prompt_example: "leading lines, a road and train rails meet at a lone robot on the horizon"

keywords.name: Lecture Hall
keywords.definition: A big university room with rows of seats rising in tiers toward the back, a lectern and screen at the front, and students listening or taking notes.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for university life, talks and learning scenes. A wide shot from the back shows the scale best.
keywords.prompt_example: "wide view of a lecture hall from the back row, students with laptops, professor at a lectern"

keywords.name: Lens Flare
keywords.definition: Light strikes the lens directly, blooming into streaks and ghosts.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for sun-kissed warmth, sci-fi shine, or dreamy interruptions.
keywords.prompt_example: "backlit runner, warm lens flare crossing frame"

keywords.name: Lensball
keywords.definition: A clear glass ball held up in front of a scene, showing a tiny upside-down copy of the world inside while the background blurs.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for magical travel shots, sunsets and landscapes with a twist. Remember the view inside the ball is flipped.
keywords.prompt_example: "lensball held up at sunset over a mountain lake, background bokeh"

keywords.name: Letterpress
keywords.definition: Old-school printing with metal or wood type pressed into thick paper, so letters sit in a slight dent with rich, slightly uneven ink.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for invitations, posters and type that looks touchable. AI can still misspell words, so keep text short.
keywords.prompt_example: "letterpress wedding invitation, cotton paper, deep debossed letters"

keywords.name: Library Study
keywords.definition: Quiet hours in a grand library: long wooden tables, green reading lamps, tall shelves of old books and a student lost in their notes.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for studying, research and calm, focused moods. Lovely for cozy video loops with drifting dust and turning pages.
keywords.prompt_example: "student taking notes at a long table in a library study, green reading lamps, tall shelves"

keywords.name: Light Leak
keywords.definition: A warm wash of light sweeps across and covers the cut.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for weddings, lifestyle and dreamy beauty edits. Best added in the edit.
keywords.prompt_example: "add in the edit: a warm light leak sweeping across the cut"

keywords.name: Light Match Cut
keywords.definition: A light flares to white, and the next shot opens on a light in the same spot.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for time jumps and dreamy montages.
keywords.prompt_example: "the lantern flares to white; the next shot is a street lamp in the same place"

keywords.name: Light Painting
keywords.definition: Drawing with a moving light in the dark while the camera shutter stays open. You get glowing ribbons, swirls and shapes hanging in the air.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for night scenes with trails of light, sparkler hearts and glowing loops around people. Words written in light often come out misspelled.
keywords.prompt_example: "person drawing glowing spirals with a flashlight on a dark beach, light painting"

keywords.name: Light Trails
keywords.definition: Smooth ribbons of light left behind by moving cars, sparklers or dancers. It looks like the light is drawing lines through the air.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for night streets, celebrations and movement. In still images it reads like a long-exposure photo; in video, expect streaks that follow motion.
keywords.prompt_example: "city bridge at night, red and white light trails"

keywords.name: Lilac Femme
keywords.definition: Soft feminine styling built around lilac and lavender tones: dreamy, gentle, unapologetically pretty.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for portraits and flat-lays that need a signature purple softness.
keywords.prompt_example: "portrait, lilac femme aesthetic"

keywords.name: Liminal Found Footage
keywords.definition: An old camcorder tape found in an empty, endless office lit by buzzing ceiling lights. The handheld camera breathes and sways, printed signs on the walls slowly go wrong, and the autofocus finds something that is gone a second later.
keywords.when_to_use: Made for creepy shorts, horror teasers and spooky storytelling. It builds dread slowly, so it does not suit upbeat or quick messages.
keywords.prompt_example: "30-second horror teaser, liminal found footage, shaky camcorder walking through an empty yellow office, signs slowly changing"

keywords.name: Line Drawing
keywords.definition: Clean continuous linework with minimal or no shading; elegance through economy.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for minimalist portraits, logos, and single-line sophistication.
keywords.prompt_example: "one line drawing of two hands"

keywords.name: Link Underline Animation
keywords.definition: When you point at a link, a line draws itself underneath from left to right, then slides away when you move off.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it for menus and text links so people can see what they are about to click. Works best with a few clear links, not long paragraphs full of them.
keywords.prompt_example: "Make my nav links show a pink underline that grows from left to right on hover and slides away when the mouse leaves."

keywords.name: Linocut
keywords.definition: A print carved into a block of lino, so you get bold chunky shapes, white gouge marks and solid flat ink.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for punchy posters, folk-style animals and bold book illustrations. Not for fine soft detail.
keywords.prompt_example: "linocut print of a fox in the snow, black ink on cream paper"

keywords.name: Liquid Mercury
keywords.definition: A silvery liquid metal that beads up into perfect, mirror-like drops and pools. It reflects everything around it.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for futuristic, sleek, otherworldly looks. Mirror surfaces pick up their surroundings, so choose a simple scene.
keywords.prompt_example: "drops of liquid mercury on black glass, studio light, macro"

keywords.name: Liquid Morph Animation
keywords.definition: One glossy liquid shape that never cuts: it flows from a drop into an icon into a product into a logo, stretching and settling like thick syrup between each form, so the whole video is one smooth take.
keywords.when_to_use: Great for logo stings, brand intros and short app promos. Only simple, bold shapes morph well, so it struggles with detailed pictures or lots of text.
keywords.prompt_example: "8-second logo sting, liquid morph animation, a glossy drop flowing into an icon then into the logo"

keywords.name: Little Red Riding Hood
keywords.definition: The girl in the red hooded cape from the old fairy tale, carrying a basket through the woods to her grandmother's house while a wolf watches. Describe the classic storybook version.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for fairy tale scenes, gentle spookiness and that iconic red against green forest. A bit of fog makes the wolf feel more mysterious.
keywords.prompt_example: "little red riding hood on a forest path, wolf eyes in the ferns, storybook illustration"

keywords.name: Live Whiteboard Lesson
keywords.definition: A lesson drawn live on one glossy whiteboard: real handwriting in proper stroke order, floating markers with no hand, a magnet that slides and an eraser that wipes, while the camera rides the pen from idea to idea.
keywords.when_to_use: Ideal for classroom-style explainers, tutorials and step-by-step how-tos. It feels like school by design, so it is not a fit for glossy ads.
keywords.prompt_example: "45-second tutorial, live whiteboard lesson animation, marker writing a diagram on a glossy whiteboard, camera following the pen"

keywords.name: Living Screencast
keywords.definition: A calm screen recording that is secretly redrawn, so it stays sharp at any zoom. The camera pushes in on the cursor, and a little pixel mascot stands on input boxes, rides sent messages and stomps buttons to show what the software is doing.
keywords.when_to_use: Made for app tutorials, feature walkthroughs and how-to reels. It takes real effort to redraw the interface, so a plain screen recording is faster for quick tips.
keywords.prompt_example: "30-second app tutorial, living screencast animation, smooth zoom on the cursor, a tiny pixel robot hopping onto the send button"

keywords.name: Lo-Fi Bedroom Studio
keywords.definition: A small, messy bedroom with a keyboard, headphones, a laptop, plants and fairy lights. Chill, homemade music vibes.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for study and chill moods, cozy illustrations and late-night creative scenes. It looks lovely as an anime-style drawing too.
keywords.prompt_example: "lo-fi bedroom studio at night, keyboard and headphones, fairy lights, rain on the window"

keywords.name: Loading Spinner
keywords.definition: A spinning ring that tells you something is working in the background. Here it finishes by turning into a tick so you know the job is done.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it for short waits of a few seconds, like saving or sending. For longer waits a progress bar or a skeleton screen tells people more.
keywords.prompt_example: "Show a clean spinning pink arc with the word Loading while the form sends, then turn it into a teal circle with a check mark and the words All done."

keywords.name: Lomography
keywords.definition: Photos from cheap toy cameras with heavy dark corners, oversaturated colors and happy little mistakes. Bold, blurry, punchy and full of character.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for playful, arty snapshots with loud color. If you want clean and sharp, this is the wrong word.
keywords.prompt_example: "lomography photo of a summer funfair, heavy vignette, saturated colors"

keywords.name: Long Exposure
keywords.definition: A slow camera that turns motion into smooth streaks: silky waterfalls, light trails, ghost crowds.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for movement, time, and calm. Water and traffic become magic.
keywords.prompt_example: "long exposure waterfall in a dark forest"

keywords.name: Long Take
keywords.definition: One unbroken shot that runs far longer than expected; no cuts, no escape.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for immersion, tension, or showcasing choreography honestly.
keywords.prompt_example: "long take through the kitchen during dinner rush"

keywords.name: Longing
keywords.definition: Wanting something just out of reach: a face pressed to a window, a hand on a closed door, someone watching a ship sail away.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for romantic, hopeful or bittersweet scenes. Put distance or glass between the person and what they want.
keywords.prompt_example: "longing, woman on a pier watching a distant ship at dusk, wind in her shawl"

keywords.name: Looking Over the Shoulder
keywords.definition: Your subject turned away but glancing back toward the camera, as if they just heard their name. It feels candid, mysterious or flirty.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for portraits and fashion shots that feel caught in a moment. Lovely with a trailing scarf or loose hair.
keywords.prompt_example: "woman looking over the shoulder at a rainy paris crosswalk, red umbrella"

keywords.name: Louis Kahn
keywords.definition: American architect (1901-1974) whose buildings feel like ancient monuments: massive concrete and brick walls, perfect circles and squares, and light pouring through huge cut-out openings.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for serious, temple-like spaces full of shadow and sunbeams. Not the right pick for cozy or playful scenes.
keywords.prompt_example: "concrete courtyard facing the ocean, Louis Kahn style, late afternoon"

keywords.name: Louis XV Armchair
keywords.definition: An 18th century French armchair with curvy cabriole legs, carved gilded wood and soft padded silk seats.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for palace rooms, fancy portraits and romantic period scenes. Pairs with pastel silks and gold.
keywords.prompt_example: "gilded Louis XV armchair in pale blue silk, palace salon"

keywords.name: Lovable Rogue
keywords.definition: A charming scoundrel with a crooked grin, quick hands and a heart of gold underneath. Rules are more like suggestions.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for adventure, heist and swashbuckling scenes. Show them mid-mischief, like picking a lock or dodging a guard, for more personality.
keywords.prompt_example: "lovable rogue grinning on a ship's rigging, golden hour"

keywords.name: Low Angle
keywords.definition: Camera looks up at the subject, lending power, menace, or myth.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to make characters loom and architecture tower.
keywords.prompt_example: "low angle on the CEO stepping from the car"

keywords.name: Low Dolly-In
keywords.definition: The camera moves slowly toward the subject from low down, about table height.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it for product shots that should feel heroic and close. Say the height, or the model may drift back up to eye level.
keywords.prompt_example: "low dolly-in at table height toward a pink ceramic cup"

keywords.name: Low-Key Lighting
keywords.definition: Mostly shadow, sparse light, high contrast; noir's native language.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for mystery, dread, and moral ambiguity.
keywords.prompt_example: "interrogation room, low-key lighting, single lamp"

keywords.name: Low Poly Art
keywords.definition: Faceted geometric rendering from early 3D: subjects built from visible triangles.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for stylized game-art scenes and crystalline landscapes.
keywords.prompt_example: "mountain landscape, low poly art"

keywords.name: Low Poly Island
keywords.definition: A tiny island made of flat faceted shapes floating in color, seen from a neat angle. Tiles rise from the sea with a splash, houses stack and trees pop up, each with a little note, and the light shows the time of day.
keywords.when_to_use: Lovely for game-style intros, calm brand worlds and build-up explainers. The simple shapes keep it cute, so it is not for realistic products.
keywords.prompt_example: "15-second build-up reel, low poly island animation, hex tiles rising from the sea with a splash, houses stacking and trees popping"

keywords.name: Low Track Into Dutch Angle
keywords.definition: A low sideways move along the ground that slowly tips the horizon into a tilt.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it to add speed and edge to cars, bikes or runners. A little tilt goes a long way; much past 15 degrees it starts to feel silly.
keywords.prompt_example: "low sideways track just above the road past a sprinting cyclist, slowly rolling into an 11 degree Dutch tilt"

keywords.name: Luis Barragan
keywords.definition: Mexican architect (1902-1988) known for smooth walls painted hot pink, sunny yellow and deep blue, with still pools of water and sharp shadows. Simple shapes, bold color, total calm.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for sunny, colorful courtyards and walls that photograph like paintings. Keep the scene uncluttered so the colors can sing.
keywords.prompt_example: "pink courtyard wall with a still pool, Luis Barragan style, midday sun"

keywords.name: Luminism
keywords.definition: 1850-70 American style of glassy light and stillness: transparent skies, mirror water, hushed glow.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for serene luminous landscapes with polished, brushless calm.
keywords.prompt_example: "bay at sunset, luminism painting"

keywords.name: Lunarpunk
keywords.definition: The nighttime sister of solarpunk, a peaceful, nature-loving future lit by moonlight, glowing plants and soft lanterns.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for mystical, calm and magical night worlds. It is a newer word, so describe the glow and moonlight too.
keywords.prompt_example: "lunarpunk village, glowing mushrooms, moonlit river"

keywords.name: -luxe
keywords.definition: From 'deluxe,' -luxe adds a polished, expensive feeling to any theme: boho luxe, night luxe, coastal luxe. Think rich fabrics, soft gold and careful styling.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for interiors, fashion and product shots that should feel high-end. On its own it can look generic, so give it a clear theme in front.
keywords.prompt_example: "desert luxe bedroom, linen, brass lamp, golden hour"

keywords.name: Lyrical Abstraction
keywords.definition: Gestural non-objective painting focused on color, brushwork, and feeling over structure.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for expressive flowing abstracts with painterly freedom.
keywords.prompt_example: "lyrical abstraction, sweeping blues and golds"

keywords.name: Macarons
keywords.definition: Small round almond cookies with smooth shells, frilly edges and a creamy filling. They come in every soft color you can imagine.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for cute, pastel dessert scenes and tea party tables. Stack them or line them up for a neat, pretty pattern.
keywords.prompt_example: "stack of pastel macarons on a marble table, soft window light"

keywords.name: Macrame
keywords.definition: Thick cotton cord knotted by hand into wall hangings, plant hangers and fringes with lots of soft texture.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for boho rooms, 1970s vibes and natural, handmade decor. Usually cream or natural colors.
keywords.prompt_example: "macrame wall hanging above a bed, trailing plants, morning sun"

keywords.name: Macro Lens
keywords.definition: An extreme close lens for tiny details and textures.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to make something small feel huge.
keywords.prompt_example: "macro shot of a raindrop sliding down a leaf"

keywords.name: Macro Photography
keywords.definition: Extreme close-up photography where tiny things fill the frame: insect eyes, dew drops, fabric weave.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for detail, texture, and wonder. Backgrounds melt into soft blur automatically.
keywords.prompt_example: "macro photography of frost on a leaf"

keywords.name: Mad Scientist
keywords.definition: A wild-haired genius in a lab coat, surrounded by bubbling flasks, sparks and strange machines. Brilliant, a bit unhinged, and always mid-experiment.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for spooky, funny or sci-fi scenes full of fun props. It leans cartoonish, so add 'realistic' if you want it grounded.
keywords.prompt_example: "mad scientist in a stone lab, glowing green flasks, lightning outside"

keywords.name: Madeleine Vionnet
keywords.definition: French designer Madeleine Vionnet (1876-1975) mastered the bias cut, cutting fabric on the diagonal so silk gowns drape, cling and flow like water, often with a Greek statue feel.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for liquid, flowing evening gowns and 1930s Hollywood-style elegance. Pairs beautifully with soft light that shows the folds.
keywords.prompt_example: "flowing bias-cut silk gown in the style of madeleine vionnet, pale champagne, marble hall"

keywords.name: Madhubani Painting
keywords.definition: A folk painting tradition from the Mithila region of Bihar, India, and nearby Nepal. Bold double outlines filled with bright color and pattern, showing fish, peacocks, gods and trees of life.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for joyful, densely patterned scenes from nature or myth. Name it directly; a vague 'Indian art' gives a muddier result.
keywords.prompt_example: "Madhubani painting of two peacocks under a tree, bright colors"

keywords.name: Magical Girl
keywords.definition: A beloved anime genre where everyday girls transform into sparkling heroines. Ribbons, wands, frills, starry light and twirling transformation poses.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for bright, hopeful heroines and transformation moments. It leans sweet and sparkly, so it's not the pick for gritty fantasy.
keywords.prompt_example: "magical girl transformation, ribbons of light, starry pink sky"

keywords.name: Magical Realism
keywords.definition: Everyday life with one quiet impossible thing in it, treated as normal. A grandmother hangs laundry while yellow butterflies follow her, and nobody blinks.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when you want gentle wonder inside a real, lived-in place. Keep the magic small and the rest ordinary, or it slides into full fantasy.
keywords.prompt_example: "magical realism, old kitchen, woman cooking while flowers grow from the stove"

keywords.name: Magnetic Art
keywords.definition: Patterns formed by magnetic force: iron filings, ferrofluid spikes, invisible fields made visible.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for scientific-abstract textures and liquid-metal forms.
keywords.prompt_example: "ferrofluid bloom, magnetic art, macro"

keywords.name: Magnetic Button
keywords.definition: A button that leans toward the mouse as it gets close, as if pulled by a magnet, then springs back when the mouse moves away. It squashes a little when clicked.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it on one main call to action, the button you most want people to press, to make it feel alive. Keep it to one or two buttons per page.
keywords.prompt_example: "Make my main button lean toward the cursor when it gets close, spring back when it leaves, and squash slightly on click"

keywords.name: Majolica
keywords.definition: Glossy pottery with a milky white glaze painted in bright yellows, blues, greens and oranges, often with flowers, fruit and swirls.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for cheerful painted plates, jugs and tiles with an Italian or Spanish feel. Busy patterns, so keep the setting simple.
keywords.prompt_example: "majolica plates with lemons and blue swirls on a white wall"

keywords.name: Mannerism
keywords.definition: Late-Renaissance elegance stretched strange: elongated figures, acidic color, sophisticated unease.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for stylized portraits with deliberate, graceful distortion.
keywords.prompt_example: "portrait with elongated neck, mannerism style"

keywords.name: Marquetry
keywords.definition: Pictures made by fitting thin slices of different colored woods together like a jigsaw on furniture or panels.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for elegant antique furniture and warm, detailed wooden artwork. Works best in close-ups.
keywords.prompt_example: "marquetry tabletop with flowers in inlaid woods, warm light"

keywords.name: Mary Cassatt
keywords.definition: (1844-1926) American Impressionist who lived in Paris and painted tender moments between mothers and children. Soft pastel colors, loose strokes and lots of warmth.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for gentle family scenes, quiet portraits and cozy home moments. Best for calm, loving subjects.
keywords.prompt_example: "mother bathing a child in a sunny room, in the style of Mary Cassatt"

keywords.name: Match Cut
keywords.definition: Two shots joined by matching shape, motion, or idea; the edit itself tells a story.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for elegant time jumps and thematic rhymes between scenes.
keywords.prompt_example: "match cut from spinning coin to spinning ferris wheel"

keywords.name: Match on Action
keywords.definition: An action starts in one shot and finishes in the next.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for energy, comedy and cause and effect.
keywords.prompt_example: "she throws the ball at the lens and it lands in the next scene"

keywords.name: Matched Zoom Transition
keywords.definition: Shot A zooms fast into a detail; shot B starts tight on the same detail in a new place and pulls back.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it for fast, smooth jumps between locations. Pick a detail both places can share, like an eye, a coin or a doorknob.
keywords.prompt_example: "shot A pushes in fast on a coffee cup rim in a cafe; shot B begins tight on the same rim at a mountain picnic and pulls back fast to reveal it"

keywords.name: Math Morph Explainer
keywords.definition: The calm style of popular math videos: a dark background, one idea on screen at a time, and shapes that smoothly morph from one concept into the next, with each idea keeping its own color.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when explaining how something works step by step, like an equation, an algorithm or how an AI model learns.
keywords.prompt_example: "dark background, a glowing curve smoothly morphs into a bar chart, math explainer animation"

keywords.name: Maximalist Interior
keywords.definition: More is more: layered patterns, bold wallpaper, stacks of books, plants, art covering every wall and bright clashing colors that somehow work.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for joyful, personality-packed rooms full of things to look at. Can turn into visual noise, so name two or three main colors.
keywords.prompt_example: "maximalist living room, jungle wallpaper, velvet sofa, gallery wall"

keywords.name: Mecha
keywords.definition: Giant piloted robots, a big part of anime for decades. Think towering armored machines with glowing visors, panel lines and thrusters.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for sci-fi scale and heroic machinery. Hands and joints can come out messy, so wide shots often look best.
keywords.prompt_example: "white mecha kneeling in a rainy hangar, glowing visor"

keywords.name: Mediterranean Villa
keywords.definition: Sun-washed white or warm plaster walls, red clay roof tiles, arched windows, terraces and bright flowers spilling over stone steps.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for holiday, summer and seaside dream homes. Pairs naturally with blue sea and strong sun.
keywords.prompt_example: "Mediterranean villa on a cliff, bougainvillea, sea view, late afternoon"

keywords.name: Medium Close-Up
keywords.definition: From the chest up: closer than a medium shot, looser than a close-up.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for conversations that should feel personal without getting in someone's face.
keywords.prompt_example: "medium close-up of him leaning in to whisper"

keywords.name: Medium Depth of Field
keywords.definition: Your subject is sharp and the background is soft, but you can still tell what is back there.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it when the setting matters but should not steal attention. If you want a dreamy blur instead, ask for shallow depth of field.
keywords.prompt_example: "medium depth of field, a robot sharp in front, the city street behind it readable but soft"

keywords.name: Medium Shot
keywords.definition: Framed roughly waist-up; the conversational workhorse of cinema.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for dialogue, interviews, and balanced everyday coverage.
keywords.prompt_example: "medium shot, she leans on the counter, talking"

keywords.name: Melancholy
keywords.definition: A soft, thoughtful sadness, like rain on a window or the last day of summer. Cool, faded colors, lowered eyes and lots of quiet space.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when you want an image to feel tender and wistful rather than tragic. Pairs naturally with overcast light and a muted palette.
keywords.prompt_example: "melancholy, girl watching rain from a train window, muted colors"

keywords.name: Memphis Animation
keywords.definition: Loud 80s design in motion: squiggles, zigzags, confetti triangles and dotted circles in bright pastels with black outlines bounce into frame, cheerful and deliberately busy.
keywords.when_to_use: Good for upbeat social reels, party promos and youthful brands. It is busy on purpose, so text needs a calm area or it gets lost.
keywords.prompt_example: "10-second promo, memphis animation, confetti triangles and squiggles bouncing in with black outlines on pastel pink"

keywords.name: Memphis Group
keywords.definition: 1980s Italian design rebellion: squiggles, clashing pastels, terrazzo, geometry with a sense of humor.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for playful retro-design scenes and postmodern pattern joy.
keywords.prompt_example: "living room, memphis group design, 1985"

keywords.name: Messy Bun
keywords.definition: Hair twisted up loosely on top of the head, with soft strands falling free. Casual, busy and comfortable.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for cozy, everyday, at-home or working scenes. It reads as informal, so skip it for formal portraits.
keywords.prompt_example: "artist with a messy bun painting at an easel, afternoon light"

keywords.name: Microgame Frenzy
keywords.definition: A rapid-fire party game film: a shouted command word, a few seconds, one action, one result, and each tiny game drawn in a totally different art style. It keeps returning to the same show stage and gets faster every round.
keywords.when_to_use: Great for speedrun reels, tool round-ups and fun list videos. It is chaotic on purpose, so it is not for anything that needs careful explaining.
keywords.prompt_example: "30-second round-up reel, microgame frenzy animation, shouted command word, quick tiny games in different art styles, speeding up each round"

keywords.name: Microscape
keywords.definition: A tiny world shot like a landscape: moss becomes forest, dew becomes lakes.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for wonder and fresh perspective. Familiar things become magical at ant scale.
keywords.prompt_example: "microscape of a mossy log, dew drops like ponds"

keywords.name: Mid-Century Cutout
keywords.definition: A 1960s cut-paper title sequence: flat, slightly wonky shapes in muted retro colors pop on and off to a swinging, jazzy rhythm, with hand-cut letters and lots of breathing room.
keywords.when_to_use: Great for stylish title sequences, event promos and retro brand spots with a jazzy track. The playful swing feels off with modern tech or very serious content.
keywords.prompt_example: "15-second title sequence, mid-century cutout animation, wonky paper shapes popping on to a jazzy beat, muted mustard and teal"

keywords.name: Mid-Century Modern
keywords.definition: The look of 1950s and 60s homes: low flat roofs, walls of glass, warm wood and open rooms that flow out to the garden.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for stylish, sunny homes with a relaxed retro feel. One of the easiest styles to get right in any model.
keywords.prompt_example: "mid-century modern house with a pool, palm trees, golden hour"

keywords.name: Mid-Laugh
keywords.definition: Caught in the middle of a real laugh, eyes squeezed, head tipped back, maybe a hand over the mouth. Natural joy that feels unposed.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when stiff smiling portraits feel fake. Teeth and eyes can look a bit strange up close, so a slightly wider shot often helps.
keywords.prompt_example: "two old friends mid-laugh at a diner booth, candid film photo"

keywords.name: Mid-Leap
keywords.definition: Your subject caught in the air at the top of a jump, feet off the ground, everything stretched out. It turns a still picture into a moment of motion.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for dancers, athletes, kids and animals full of energy. Hands and feet can get odd in tricky poses, so try a few versions.
keywords.prompt_example: "ballet dancer mid-leap over a puddle, city street, golden hour"

keywords.name: Middle-Aged
keywords.definition: Roughly between 40 and 60, with gentle signs of age like a few grey hairs and soft lines. A simple way to stop the AI from making everyone look 25.
keywords.when_to_use: Use whenever age matters to the story. For more precision, give a decade, like 'in her fifties.'
keywords.prompt_example: "middle-aged teacher grading papers at a kitchen table, lamplight"

keywords.name: Ludwig Mies van der Rohe
keywords.definition: German-American architect (1886-1969) famous for the motto 'less is more.' Glass walls, thin steel frames and open floors so simple they almost disappear.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for quiet, elegant glass pavilions and towers. There is not much ornament here, so the light and setting do the work.
keywords.prompt_example: "glass house in a snowy meadow, Mies van der Rohe style, morning light"

keywords.name: Miniature
keywords.definition: Everything looks tiny and handmade, like a scale model or a toy town you could hold in your hands.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to make big scenes feel cute and collectible. Real people can end up looking like little figurines, which is part of the charm.
keywords.prompt_example: "miniature Paris cafe on a fingertip, macro photography"

keywords.name: Minimal Web Design
keywords.definition: A stripped-back site with lots of white space, clean type and very little color, so your eye goes straight to what matters.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for portfolios, premium products and focused tools. Needs good photos or writing, because there is nothing else to hide behind.
keywords.prompt_example: "portfolio for a ceramic artist, minimal web design, white page, one large photo"

keywords.name: Mixed Media
keywords.definition: Multiple materials in one work: paint over collage over ink over fabric.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for layered, tactile compositions that resist a single technique.
keywords.prompt_example: "portrait, mixed media, paint and newspaper collage"

keywords.name: Modal Dialog
keywords.definition: A box that pops up in the middle of the screen while the page behind it goes dark. It asks one question and waits for an answer, usually with two buttons.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it to confirm something important, like deleting a list. Keep it rare, because a box that blocks the whole page gets annoying fast.
keywords.prompt_example: "Add a modal dialog that asks Delete this list? with Cancel and Delete buttons, dims the page behind it and pops in with a small bounce"

keywords.name: Model Train Layout
keywords.definition: A tiny world on a tabletop: miniature trains winding past little towns, tunnels, trees and lakes. Everything looks small, careful and loved.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for charming miniature scenes or a nostalgic hobby room. Add macro photography to sell the tiny scale.
keywords.prompt_example: "model train layout with a snowy mountain village, warm lamp light"

keywords.name: Modern Farmhouse
keywords.definition: White walls, wooden beams, shiplap boards, a big farm sink and black metal lights. Country charm, kept clean and simple.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for warm family kitchens and homey living rooms. It is very familiar, so add one surprise to keep it from feeling generic.
keywords.prompt_example: "modern farmhouse kitchen, wood beams, farm sink, morning light"

keywords.name: Modern Serif Web Design
keywords.definition: A polished, up-to-date site with elegant IBM Plex Serif type, a small palette and clean, calm layouts.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for software products, studios and services that want to feel thoughtful and trustworthy. May feel too quiet for loud, fun brands.
keywords.prompt_example: "homepage for a note-taking app, modern serif web design, soft grey, serif headline"

keywords.name: Monochrome Component Kit UI
keywords.definition: A minimal black, white and grey app look made of clean ready-made pieces like buttons, cards and menus, set in the crisp Geist font.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for software apps, dashboards and developer tools when you want something tidy fast. So popular that it can look like every other new app.
keywords.prompt_example: "settings page for a habit tracker app, monochrome component kit ui, black and white cards and toggles"

keywords.name: Monochrome Outfit
keywords.definition: An outfit in a single color from head to toe, like all camel, all lilac or all black, mixing different shades and textures of that one color.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for striking fashion images and clean product shots. Name the color clearly, and a matching background makes it even bolder.
keywords.prompt_example: "model in an all lilac monochrome outfit against a lilac backdrop"

keywords.name: Monospace Hacker Web Design
keywords.definition: A compact, high-contrast site set entirely in Space Mono, a typewriter-like font where every letter takes the same space, with a dark, hacker-chic mood.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for developer tools, tech clubs, newsletters and coding communities. Feels too technical for lifestyle or family brands.
keywords.prompt_example: "newsletter site for a coding club, monospace hacker web design, white mono text on black"

keywords.name: Monotype
keywords.definition: A one-off print made by painting on a smooth plate and pressing paper onto it, giving soft, smudgy, painterly marks.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for moody, loose, one-of-a-kind art prints. Expect a dreamy, imperfect finish, not crisp lines.
keywords.prompt_example: "monotype print of a figure by the sea, smudgy gray and blue ink"

keywords.name: Monsoon Rain
keywords.definition: Heavy, dramatic, warm rain. Sheets of water, glossy streets, life carrying on under umbrellas.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for drama and atmosphere in city or tropical scenes. Reflections double the beauty.
keywords.prompt_example: "market street in monsoon rain, umbrellas glowing"

keywords.name: Monstera
keywords.definition: A big, glossy houseplant with heart-shaped leaves full of splits and holes. Tropical, bold and very photogenic.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for jungle interiors, modern plant corners and leafy shadow patterns. Its leaf shape is easy for AI to get right.
keywords.prompt_example: "monstera plant in a sunny corner, leaf shadows on a white wall"

keywords.name: Moorish Architecture
keywords.definition: Palaces and courtyards from Islamic Spain and North Africa, with horseshoe arches, carved plaster lace, patterned tiles and quiet fountains.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for rich, peaceful courtyards and palace halls full of pattern. Be respectful and specific about place when it matters to your story.
keywords.prompt_example: "Moorish courtyard with horseshoe arches and a tiled fountain, soft afternoon light"

keywords.name: Mori Kei
keywords.definition: Forest-girl fashion: layered natural fabrics, earthy tones, dressed like you live in the woods gently.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for soft woodland portraits and slow-living scenes.
keywords.prompt_example: "portrait in a birch forest, mori kei fashion"

keywords.name: Morph
keywords.definition: One scene smoothly reshapes into another.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for signature dream moments. Far easier in AI video than in traditional effects.
keywords.prompt_example: "the paper crane slowly reshapes into a white bird"

keywords.name: Mosaic
keywords.definition: Pictures made from hundreds of tiny tiles, glass or broken pottery pieces set side by side, with thin lines of grout between them.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for floors, walls, fountains and ancient or playful murals. Faces can get blocky, which is part of the charm.
keywords.prompt_example: "mosaic of a peacock made from broken colorful tiles, sunlit wall"

keywords.name: Moss Covered
keywords.definition: Soft green growth blanketing stone, wood, or forgotten things. Nature quietly taking over.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for enchanted forests, ruins, and anything that should feel ancient and alive.
keywords.prompt_example: "moss covered stone stairway into a forest"

keywords.name: Motivated Lighting
keywords.definition: Cinematic light that pretends to come from the scene's own sources, enhanced invisibly.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for polished realism where the lighting has an alibi.
keywords.prompt_example: "moonlight through blinds, motivated lighting"
