keywords.name: Movement Match Montage
keywords.definition: The same movement repeated in different places, with each cut landing in the middle of the move.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it for montages that need rhythm and a feeling that it is all one story. Ask for the same height and size in frame each time.
keywords.prompt_example: "a montage of a girl making the same jump on a beach, a rooftop and a forest path, each cut landing mid-jump at the same height in frame"

keywords.name: Multiple Exposure
keywords.definition: Several pictures layered into one frame, so faces, cities and nature blend together like a memory.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for dreamy, emotional, story-filled images. Keep each layer simple, or the result turns into a busy jumble.
keywords.prompt_example: "multiple exposure of a woman's profile, a pine forest and a city skyline"

keywords.name: Mustard Yellow
keywords.definition: A warm, slightly brown yellow, softer than lemon and richer than butter. Very vintage, very cozy.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for retro fashion, 70s rooms and warm autumn feels. It can look muddy next to gray, so pair it with blue, teal or burgundy.
keywords.prompt_example: "mustard yellow armchair in a retro living room"

keywords.name: Muted Palette
keywords.definition: Colors with the volume turned down: dusty, greyed, quiet tones. Sophisticated and calm.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when bright colors feel cheap or loud. Editorial and interior content loves this.
keywords.prompt_example: "muted palette living room, linen and clay tones"

keywords.name: Mythological
keywords.definition: Gods, monsters, and legends rendered with epic-narrative weight.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for grand mythic scenes across any culture's canon.
keywords.prompt_example: "sea god rising from waves, mythological painting"

keywords.name: Naive
keywords.definition: Untrained-artist charm: flattened perspective, honest color, sincerity over technique.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for folk-warm scenes that should feel handmade and heartfelt.
keywords.prompt_example: "village festival, naive art painting"

keywords.name: Naturaleza
keywords.definition: Lush nature-first styling: abundant flora, organic shapes, celebration of living green.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for verdant scenes where nature is the whole point.
keywords.prompt_example: "overgrown greenhouse, naturaleza style"

keywords.name: Naturalist Field Journal
keywords.definition: A nature explorer's sketchbook: watercolor studies of birds, leaves and insects, handwritten notes, pressed flowers and dates in the margins.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for nature study, cozy adventure and science-meets-art pages. Lovely with watercolor and botanical styles; the writing is decorative only.
keywords.prompt_example: "naturalist field journal page with watercolor sketches of birds and pressed ferns, handwritten notes"

keywords.name: Nature Documentary
keywords.definition: The patient look of a wildlife film: long lens, soft background, animals going about their day, and the feeling that someone waited hours for this one shot.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to make any creature, even a tiny or made-up one, feel real and observed. Works best when the animal looks unaware of the camera.
keywords.prompt_example: "nature documentary shot of a fox kit pouncing in snow, telephoto lens"

keywords.name: Needlepoint
keywords.definition: Tiny even stitches of wool worked across a stiff canvas grid, filling every space to make a soft, pixel-like picture.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for cushions, vintage samplers and cozy grandma-chic decor. The grid gives a slightly blocky look.
keywords.prompt_example: "needlepoint cushion with a pug and roses, wool stitches, armchair"

keywords.name: Neko
keywords.definition: Cat-eared characters and feline motifs from Japanese pop culture.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for playful anime-adjacent character designs.
keywords.prompt_example: "neko girl character, anime style"

keywords.name: Neo Dada
keywords.definition: 1950s-60s revival of dada mischief: everyday objects, irony, and anti-art gestures.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for conceptual collage and duchampian humor.
keywords.prompt_example: "sculpture of a painted tire, neo dada"

keywords.name: Neo Gothic
keywords.definition: Gothic architecture and mood revived with modern drama: pointed arches, tracery, contemporary darkness.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for architecture, interiors, or portraits that need cathedral-scale atmosphere.
keywords.prompt_example: "cathedral interior, neo gothic style"

keywords.name: Neo-Rococo
keywords.definition: Rococo's frills revived with modern self-awareness: pastel excess, ornamental overload, wink included.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for playful ornate interiors and fashion with maximalist charm.
keywords.prompt_example: "boudoir interior, neo-rococo, pastel gilt"

keywords.name: Neobrutalism Web Design
keywords.definition: A friendlier take on brutalism: thick black borders, chunky offset shadows, bright accent colors and raw, boxy layouts on warm off-white backgrounds.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for startups, creative tools, indie products and youthful brands. Can look loud and crowded if every element gets a border.
keywords.prompt_example: "pricing page for a sticker shop, neobrutalism web design, thick black borders, hot pink and lime"

keywords.name: Neon Glow
keywords.definition: Electric, colorful light like city signs at night. Pinks, blues, and purples bouncing off wet streets and faces.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for nightlife, retro-future vibes, or anything that should feel electric and modern.
keywords.prompt_example: "ramen stall at midnight, neon glow"

keywords.name: Neon Noir
keywords.definition: Noir updated in saturated neon: wet streets reflecting pink and cyan signage.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for modern night-city stories with electric melancholy.
keywords.prompt_example: "rain-slick alley, neon noir grade"

keywords.name: Neon Web Design
keywords.definition: Electric glowing colors like neon signs, bright pinks, blues and greens on dark backgrounds, with bold contrast that pops off the screen.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for nightlife, gaming, music and events. Glow effects get tiring and hard to read in big blocks of text.
keywords.prompt_example: "event page for a roller disco, neon web design, pink and blue glow on black"

keywords.name: Neumorphism UI
keywords.definition: Soft buttons and cards that look pressed into, or pushed out of, the same smooth surface, using light and dark shadows on a single background color.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for calm control panels, music players and smart home apps. Low contrast makes buttons hard for some people to see, so use it with care.
keywords.prompt_example: "smart home thermostat app, neumorphism ui, soft grey buttons pushed out of the surface"

keywords.name: New Romantic
keywords.definition: 1980s flamboyant glamour: ruffles, drama makeup, synth-pop theatricality.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for bold retro fashion portraits with stage presence.
keywords.prompt_example: "portrait, new romantic fashion, 1981"

keywords.name: Night Luxe
keywords.definition: After-dark glamour: champagne gold on black, city lights, velvet ropes and expensive shadows.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for nightlife scenes, luxury branding, and evening-event moods.
keywords.prompt_example: "rooftop bar at night, night luxe aesthetic"

keywords.name: Noir Grade
keywords.definition: Deep blacks, silver highlights, venetian-blind shadows; crime cinema's monochrome soul.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for detective stories and moral shadow, color optional.
keywords.prompt_example: "office at night, noir grade, blinds shadow"

keywords.name: Northern Lights
keywords.definition: Ribbons of green, and sometimes pink and purple, light rippling across a dark polar sky. Nature's own light show.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for magical night landscapes and quiet wonder. Snowy ground and a still lake for reflections make it shine.
keywords.prompt_example: "northern lights over a snowy cabin, green ribbons reflected in a lake"

keywords.name: Nostalgia
keywords.definition: That warm ache for the past: faded photos, sunlit bedrooms, old toys and summer afternoons that seem to last forever.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to make a scene feel like a cherished memory. Pairs well with film looks and soft, golden light.
keywords.prompt_example: "nostalgia, kids on bikes at dusk, faded film photo, warm light"

keywords.name: Notification Badge
keywords.definition: A small bright circle with a number that sits on the corner of an icon, like a bell, to show how many new things are waiting. It pops in, counts up and clears once you look.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it to point gently at new messages or updates. Too many badges at once start to feel like nagging, so save it for things that matter.
keywords.prompt_example: "Put a pink count badge on the bell icon in the header that pops in with a little bounce, makes the bell wiggle as the number goes up, and clears when I click the bell."

keywords.name: Number Counter
keywords.definition: Big numbers on stat cards count up quickly from zero to their real values and slow down as they land.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it to make key numbers, like customers or ratings, catch the eye. Use real numbers only; a counting animation will not make a weak stat look stronger.
keywords.prompt_example: "Add three stat cards whose numbers count up from zero to 12,000+, 98% and 4.9 when they come into view, easing out at the end."

keywords.name: Object-Oriented Ontology
keywords.definition: Philosophy-flavored art where things have inner lives: objects depicted as if they matter without us.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for uncanny still lifes where the furniture seems to be thinking.
keywords.prompt_example: "portrait of a chair alone in a field, object-oriented ontology"

keywords.name: Object Portal
keywords.definition: A ring, frame or lens held up to the camera shows the next scene inside it, and the camera pushes through.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to move into a new place or world in one playful move.
keywords.prompt_example: "a ring held up to the lens frames the beach; the camera pushes through it"

keywords.name: Octane Render
keywords.definition: A glossy, ultra-clean 3D look with crisp reflections and soft, believable light. Everything looks freshly made and expensive.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when you want polished 3D art, toys or products that shine. It can feel a bit too perfect, so add texture words if you want warmth.
keywords.prompt_example: "glass perfume bottle on wet black stone, octane render"

keywords.name: Oil Painting
keywords.definition: Rich, layered classical paint with visible brushwork and deep color. The museum look.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for portraits, drama, and timelessness. Instantly makes a scene feel important.
keywords.prompt_example: "oil painting of a woman with pink hair, dark background"

keywords.name: Ominous
keywords.definition: Something bad is coming. Heavy skies, long shadows, and quiet tension.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for thrillers, storms, and drama. It darkens mood without adding gore.
keywords.prompt_example: "ominous farmhouse under a green storm sky"

keywords.name: One Line Drawing Animation
keywords.definition: One warm black ink line that never leaves the paper, drawn live while the camera follows the pen. At the end the camera pulls back to show every little scene was part of one big picture.
keywords.when_to_use: Beautiful for brand stories, life journeys and thoughtful explainers. It is slow and minimal, so it is not built for lots of facts or text.
keywords.prompt_example: "30-second brand story, one line drawing animation, a single ink line drawing a journey as the camera follows the pen, then pulls back"

keywords.name: Ontology
keywords.definition: Being itself as subject: stark philosophical compositions about existence and thing-ness.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for minimal conceptual pieces with quiet existential weight.
keywords.prompt_example: "single door standing in a field, ontological art"

keywords.name: Opal
keywords.definition: A milky or dark gemstone that flashes little patches of rainbow color as it moves, like fire trapped inside. No two look the same.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for magical, dreamy jewelry and fantasy treasure. Close-ups show the color play best; small stones in wide shots can turn plain white.
keywords.prompt_example: "opal ring flashing blue and green fire, macro shot on black velvet"

keywords.name: Open-Plan Office
keywords.definition: A big, bright office with no walls between desks: long tables, laptops, plants, big windows and people working side by side.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for company websites, hiring pages and work culture scenes. Ask for candid, real people to avoid stiff stock-photo poses.
keywords.prompt_example: "open-plan office with plants and big windows, team working at long desks, morning light"

keywords.name: Opulent
keywords.definition: Extreme, unapologetic luxury. Gold, marble, abundance stacked on abundance.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for wealth, fantasy palaces, and maximalist beauty.
keywords.prompt_example: "opulent banquet table, gold candelabras, marble hall"

keywords.name: Orbit
keywords.definition: The camera circles the subject, holding them centered while the world wheels behind.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for hero moments, product beauty passes, and dizzying emotional peaks.
keywords.prompt_example: "slow orbit around the dancers, lights streaking behind"

keywords.name: Orchestra Pit
keywords.definition: A sunken space in front of a theater stage, packed with musicians, music stands and little lamps. Elegant and a bit hidden.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for grand theater nights and classical music scenes. Shoot from above to show the rows of players.
keywords.prompt_example: "orchestra pit from above, small stand lamps, velvet theater seats"

keywords.name: Organic Abstraction
keywords.definition: Abstract forms borrowed from nature: cells, seeds, currents, growth without literal subjects.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for soft biomorphic compositions and nature-adjacent abstracts.
keywords.prompt_example: "organic abstraction, seed forms, cream and sage"

keywords.name: Origami
keywords.definition: Folded paper that comes to life: flat squares crease along sharp lines and fold into birds, boats or icons, each face catching a different shade from one soft light. Every reveal is a fold, never a fade.
keywords.when_to_use: Nice for calm explainers, logo reveals and brands about ideas taking shape. Folds take time to read, so it is too slow for rapid-fire edits.
keywords.prompt_example: "8-second logo reveal, origami animation, a white paper square folding step by step into a crane"

keywords.name: Orphism
keywords.definition: Early abstraction of luminous color circles and prisms; cubism gone chromatic.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for radiant geometric abstracts built on color relationships.
keywords.prompt_example: "concentric color circles, orphism"

keywords.name: Oscar Niemeyer
keywords.definition: Brazilian architect (1907-2012) who bent white concrete into sweeping curves, domes and bowls. His buildings look like sculptures floating on reflecting pools.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for bright, graceful modern buildings with a tropical, optimistic feel. Pairs beautifully with big skies and water.
keywords.prompt_example: "curved white concrete chapel by a lake, Oscar Niemeyer style, blue sky"

keywords.name: Over-the-Shoulder
keywords.definition: Framed past one character's shoulder onto another; conversation with built-in geography.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for dialogue scenes needing connection and spatial clarity.
keywords.prompt_example: "over-the-shoulder shot as she confronts him"

keywords.name: Overcast Light
keywords.definition: The soft, even light of a cloudy day. No harsh shadows, no squinting. Very flattering and calm.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for gentle, honest scenes and soft product shots. Great when harsh shadows keep ruining your image.
keywords.prompt_example: "woman reading on a porch, overcast light"

keywords.name: Overgrown Ruins
keywords.definition: Old buildings swallowed by nature, with vines, trees and moss growing through broken walls and windows.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for peaceful after-the-end worlds, lost temples and quiet adventure. Add light like golden hour or fog to set the feeling.
keywords.prompt_example: "overgrown ruins of a train station, vines, soft sunbeams"

keywords.name: Oversized Streetwear
keywords.definition: Baggy hoodies, roomy cargo pants, big puffer jackets and chunky sneakers, worn loose and layered. Relaxed, cool and very city.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for urban portraits, skate parks and music videos. Avoid brand names; describe colors and pieces instead.
keywords.prompt_example: "teen in oversized streetwear, baggy hoodie and cargo pants, graffiti alley"

keywords.name: Oxidized Iron
keywords.definition: Iron eaten by rust into flaky orange, brown and red layers. Rough, gritty and full of age.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for abandoned places, industrial textures and gritty moods. It pairs well with grey skies and decay.
keywords.prompt_example: "rusty oxidized iron gate, peeling texture, overcast day"

keywords.name: Page Transition
keywords.definition: When you click a link, a coloured panel sweeps across the screen and the next page appears behind it, instead of a sudden jump.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it to make a site feel smooth and connected, like one continuous space. Keep it quick, around half a second, so it never slows people down.
keywords.prompt_example: "Add a page transition: when I click a link, a pink panel wipes across the screen and reveals the new page, and it wipes back the other way when I go back."

keywords.name: Pagination
keywords.definition: A row of numbered page buttons with previous and next arrows under a list. The current page is highlighted, and clicking a number jumps to that page of results.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it when a list is too long for one screen and people like to know where they are, like search results or a shop. For casual browsing, endless scrolling can feel smoother.
keywords.prompt_example: "Split this product grid into pages of 9 with numbered page buttons and next and previous arrows, and slide a pink highlight to the current page."

keywords.name: Paisley
keywords.definition: Curving teardrop shapes packed with tiny swirls and flowers. The motif came from Persia and India, and was named after the Scottish town that wove it into shawls.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for rich textiles, bandanas, wallpaper and boho fashion. It gets busy fast, so give it room or limit the colors.
keywords.prompt_example: "silk scarf with red and gold paisley, flat lay"

keywords.name: Palette Knife
keywords.definition: Paint spread with a flat metal knife instead of a brush, leaving smooth, chunky slabs of color with sharp edges. Bold and almost sculpted.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for bright landscapes, city lights and flowers with lots of energy. Fine detail gets lost, so think in big shapes.
keywords.prompt_example: "rainy city street at night, palette knife painting"

keywords.name: Palimpsest Art
keywords.definition: Layered surfaces where earlier marks ghost through newer ones: history visible in the overwrite.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for aged, story-laden textures and archaeological depth.
keywords.prompt_example: "wall of layered posters and paint, palimpsest art"

keywords.name: Pan
keywords.definition: The camera stays in one spot and turns left or right, like turning your head.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to follow someone across a room, or to reveal what is beside them.
keywords.prompt_example: "slow pan right across the busy market"

keywords.name: Pan Onto Subject
keywords.definition: The camera turns from somewhere else and comes to rest on your subject.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it for a small reveal, or to guide the eye to your hero. Keep it slow, because a fast version starts to look like a whip pan.
keywords.prompt_example: "the camera pans across a kitchen shelf and settles on a pink cup"

keywords.name: Pan-Through World Change
keywords.definition: One continuous sideways pan where the vehicle and the world change each time the subject passes behind a pillar.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it for playful journeys or product adventures. Give each world a clear, different look so every change reads.
keywords.prompt_example: "one continuous side-on pan following a cyclist; behind each pillar the bike and the world change, from city to desert to snowy village"

keywords.name: Pancake Stack
keywords.definition: A tall, fluffy tower of pancakes with butter melting on top and syrup running down the sides. Breakfast at its happiest.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for cheerful morning scenes and indulgent food shots. Add syrup drizzle for that sticky, mouthwatering moment.
keywords.prompt_example: "tall pancake stack, melting butter, syrup drizzle, sunny kitchen"

keywords.name: Panel Grid
keywords.definition: A page split into neat comic boxes, each showing a moment in order, like a little storyboard. Reading left to right, the story moves along.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when you want a short sequence or a mini story in one image. Ask for three or four panels, more often gets confusing.
keywords.prompt_example: "four panel grid comic, cat trying to catch a fish, simple ink"

keywords.name: Papel Picado
keywords.definition: Mexican tissue paper banners with delicate cut-out flowers, birds and skulls, strung in bright rows overhead.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for festive streets, celebrations and Dia de los Muertos scenes. It is part of real family traditions, so keep the setting joyful and respectful.
keywords.prompt_example: "village plaza strung with papel picado banners, warm evening light"

keywords.name: Paper and Neon
keywords.definition: Soft cut-paper shapes lit up by glowing neon tubes, so the cozy and the electric sit side by side.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for night scenes, signs and dreamy city art with a handmade touch. It works best in dark settings where the glow can show.
keywords.prompt_example: "cut paper city skyline with pink neon outlines, night"

keywords.name: Paper Cut Lightbox
keywords.definition: A layered paper shadow box lit from behind: sheets of cut card stacked in a shallow box, warm light glowing through the paper, windows and moons shining through holes. Layers slide and pivot like paper on sticks, and the lamp turning on is the big moment.
keywords.when_to_use: Gorgeous for bedtime stories, holiday cards and cozy brand moments. Paper only slides and turns, so it cannot do bendy, stretchy action.
keywords.prompt_example: "15-second holiday card, paper cut lightbox animation, layered paper village glowing from behind, lamp turning on, windows lighting one by one"

keywords.name: Paper Map Journey
keywords.definition: A journey told on a paper map: a dashed route draws itself from place to place, pins drop with a little bounce, place names stamp on, and the camera glides and tilts to follow the line.
keywords.when_to_use: Great for travel stories, company histories, delivery routes and event recaps. It needs a real route with a few clear stops, or there is nothing to follow.
keywords.prompt_example: "20-second travel story, paper map journey animation, dashed route drawing across an old map, pins bouncing in at each city"

keywords.name: Paper Storybook
keywords.definition: A warm handmade picture book where every character and prop is a paper sticker with a white border, layered on textured paper. Stickers peel on with a little bounce, timed to the narrator's words, and everything gently wiggles like stop motion.
keywords.when_to_use: Lovely for gentle story explainers, kids' content and cozy brand stories with a voiceover. It is slow and sweet, so it will not suit fast, hard-selling ads.
keywords.prompt_example: "30-second story explainer, paper storybook animation, sticker characters peeling onto textured paper as the narrator speaks"

keywords.name: Paper Texture Web Design
keywords.definition: A site that feels like real printed paper, with soft paper grain, very few colors and a clean mix of Montserrat and Roboto type.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for stationery shops, writers, studios and handmade brands. The texture can look dull if the content is thin.
keywords.prompt_example: "website for a stationery shop, paper texture web design, cream paper grain, black ink"

keywords.name: Papercraft
keywords.definition: Scenes built from cut, folded, and layered paper. Handmade, dimensional, and charming.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for playful explainers, craft aesthetics, and gentle 3D without computer-render coldness.
keywords.prompt_example: "papercraft diorama of a lighthouse in a storm"

keywords.name: Parallax Scrolling
keywords.definition: Layers of a page move at different speeds as you scroll, so the background drifts slowly while the front races past. It makes a flat page feel deep, like looking out of a train window.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it on a hero, the big opening area of a page, to give a landing page a sense of depth. Keep it gentle: strong movement can make some people feel queasy.
keywords.prompt_example: "Add a parallax hero with a sky, far hills and near hills that each move at a different speed as I scroll"

keywords.name: Parchment Editorial UI
keywords.definition: Pages that look printed on warm ivory parchment, with near-black ink, calm editorial type and just one earthy clay accent used sparingly. It feels like a thoughtful research journal.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for writing tools, research sites, essays and thoughtful knowledge products. Too quiet for flashy sales pages or kids' apps.
keywords.prompt_example: "reading app for long essays, parchment editorial ui, ivory paper, near-black ink, one clay accent"

keywords.name: Pareidolia
keywords.definition: Faces and figures hiding in things: clouds, bark, sockets that stare back.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for playful or eerie hidden-image compositions.
keywords.prompt_example: "forest where trees form faces, pareidolia"

keywords.name: Party Kei
keywords.definition: Sparkly Japanese-inspired party fashion: sequins, tulle, plastic jewelry, celebration as a lifestyle.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for festive fashion portraits that glitter without irony.
keywords.prompt_example: "birthday portrait, party kei style"

keywords.name: Pasta Art
keywords.definition: Artwork built from actual pasta shapes: macaroni mosaics, spaghetti linework, farfalle flourishes.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for playful food art, craft-project textures, or delightfully absurd portraits.
keywords.prompt_example: "portrait of a cat made of pasta, pasta art"

keywords.name: Pastel Academia
keywords.definition: The academia look with the contrast turned soft: cream blazers, mint notebooks, gentle study light.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for approachable scholarly scenes without dark academia's gloom.
keywords.prompt_example: "study desk, pastel academia"

keywords.name: Pastel Palette
keywords.definition: Soft, milky, gentle colors: baby pink, mint, lavender, cream. Sweet and calming.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for gentle, dreamy, friendly content. The default palette of soft aesthetics.
keywords.prompt_example: "pastel palette bakery storefront, morning light"

keywords.name: Peacock
keywords.definition: A bird with a giant fan of green and blue tail feathers, each one marked with a shimmering eye. Pure color and showing off.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when you want jewel colors and drama in one word. Ask for tail fanned out if you want the full display.
keywords.prompt_example: "peacock with tail fanned out in a palace garden, jewel tones"

keywords.name: Pearls
keywords.definition: Smooth, round gems grown inside oysters and mussels, with a soft, glowing shine. They come in white, cream, pink, gold and dark grey, and in lumpy shapes called baroque pearls.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for classic elegance on necklaces, earrings and hair pieces. Add "baroque pearls" for irregular shapes with a more artistic feel.
keywords.prompt_example: "woman wearing a long strand of cream pearls, black dress, soft studio light"

keywords.name: Pedestal
keywords.definition: The whole camera rises or lowers straight up and down, without tilting.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to rise above a scene and show its layout, or to drop down to eye level.
keywords.prompt_example: "the camera pedestals up from the table into a top-down view"

keywords.name: Pedestal Down
keywords.definition: The whole camera lowers straight down without tilting.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it to land on a subject or drop to its eye level. Some models tilt instead of lowering, so say straight down.
keywords.prompt_example: "the camera lowers straight down to the height of a pink cup on a table"

keywords.name: Pencil Sketch Web Design
keywords.definition: A friendly hand-drawn site that looks like pencil drawings on warm cream paper, with soft teal accents, handwritten headings, dashed card outlines and chunky pencil-style shadows.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for creative classes, kids' learning, journaling apps and small makers. Can feel unfinished for serious finance or health brands.
keywords.prompt_example: "website for a drawing class, pencil sketch web design, cream paper, teal accents, dashed outlines"

keywords.name: Penny Dreadful
keywords.definition: The cheap, thrilling story papers of Victorian England, full of villains, ghosts and highwaymen. Picture inky woodcut-style illustrations and lurid, shouting headlines.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for spooky, sensational Victorian scenes with a printed, pulpy feel. It is rough on purpose, so do not expect polished detail.
keywords.prompt_example: "penny dreadful cover, cloaked villain in foggy London alley, woodcut style"

keywords.name: Persian Miniature
keywords.definition: Small, richly detailed paintings made for illustrated books in Persia, today's Iran. Flat, layered spaces, jewel colors, patterned carpets and gardens, often edged in gold.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for storytelling scenes full of tiny figures, palaces and gardens. It doesn't do deep, realistic perspective, and that's part of its beauty.
keywords.prompt_example: "Persian miniature of a garden gathering with musicians, gold border"

keywords.name: Perspective Depth Web Design
keywords.definition: A site that breaks out of flatness with isometric views (3D seen from a tilted angle), vanishing points and stacked layers that pull your eye through the page.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for tech products, games, architecture and product tours. Can be heavy to build and slow on older phones.
keywords.prompt_example: "product tour for a smart city app, perspective depth web design, isometric buildings, layered cards"

keywords.name: Petite
keywords.definition: A shorter, small-framed body. Clothes and furniture look a little bigger around them, and they read clearly as an adult, not a child.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to show shorter adults in fashion, office and everyday scenes. Add an age or role, like "petite woman in her forties", so the AI keeps them grown up.
keywords.prompt_example: "petite woman in her forties in a tailored blazer, city crosswalk"

keywords.name: Pewter
keywords.definition: A soft, dull grey metal with a gentle, low shine, often seen in old mugs, plates and candlesticks. Quiet and old-world.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for medieval feasts, rustic tables and muted still lifes. It is less flashy than silver, which is the point.
keywords.prompt_example: "pewter tankards and candlesticks on a rough wooden table"

keywords.name: Phantastische Kunst
keywords.definition: Early-20th-century German fantastic art: dreamlike, meticulous, quietly unsettling visions.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for detailed dream imagery with old-world craft.
keywords.prompt_example: "dream city on a hill, phantastische kunst"

keywords.name: Photorealism
keywords.definition: Painting or rendering so precise it reads as photograph; craft as spectacle.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when you want painted subjects with camera-level fidelity.
keywords.prompt_example: "street scene, photorealism, oil on canvas"

keywords.name: Pictogram Motion
keywords.definition: A sports-event style flash-card film: each card is one faceless stick-figure symbol doing one action on a big sun circle, with a huge heavy title and a small index number, over a grid pattern whose rows slide. Every cut lands on a drum hit.
keywords.when_to_use: Great for lists, step-by-step tips and sporty, energetic brand reels. Each card holds one idea only, so it is not for long explanations.
keywords.prompt_example: "15-second tips reel, pictogram motion, faceless figure icons on a big sun disc, heavy titles, cuts landing on every drum hit"

keywords.name: Pieter Bruegel the Elder
keywords.definition: (c. 1525-1569) Flemish painter of busy village life seen from above: peasant weddings, frozen ponds full of skaters and snowy hunters coming home. Earthy colors and many tiny people.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for lively crowd scenes and wintry old village landscapes. Faces are small and simple, so it is not for portraits.
keywords.prompt_example: "snowy village with skaters on a frozen pond, in the style of Pieter Bruegel the Elder"

keywords.name: Pinhole Camera
keywords.definition: A tiny hole instead of a lens, giving soft, dreamy pictures with dark edges and everything gently in focus.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for quiet, timeless and slightly ghostly images. Nothing is sharp, so it is not the choice for crisp detail.
keywords.prompt_example: "pinhole camera photo of an old pier at dawn, soft vignette"

keywords.name: Pink Parisian
keywords.definition: Paris dipped in rose: pink cafes, macarons, wrought-iron balconies at blush hour.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for travel-fantasy scenes and feminine city romance.
keywords.prompt_example: "cafe terrace, pink parisian aesthetic"

keywords.name: Pinocchio
keywords.definition: The wooden puppet from the original 1883 Italian story, carved by an old woodcarver, with a nose that grows when he lies. In the book he is a cheeky troublemaker in a paper suit and bark shoes. Describe the book version, not later cartoon versions.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for storybook mischief, workshops full of wood shavings and fairy tale lessons. Ask for 'carved wood texture' to keep him a real puppet.
keywords.prompt_example: "pinocchio from the 1883 italian story, wooden puppet in a paper suit, cluttered woodcarver's workshop"

keywords.name: Pixel Arcade UI
keywords.definition: A playful arcade game interface built on the VT323 pixel font, sharp right-angle corners, chunky buttons that press down into solid blocks, and cards trimmed with rainbow shadows like an arcade cabinet.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for game sites, gaming communities, retro events and fun app menus. Pixel type gets tiring in long text.
keywords.prompt_example: "game menu screen for a racing game, pixel arcade ui, chunky pressable buttons, rainbow trim"

keywords.name: Pixel Cutie
keywords.definition: Chunky pixel-art rendering of adorable subjects: 16-bit pets, hearts, and sparkles.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for game-style icons, stickers, and nostalgic cute graphics.
keywords.prompt_example: "pixel cutie kitten, 16-bit sprite"

keywords.name: Pixel Diorama
keywords.definition: Flat pixel-art characters standing like paper cutouts inside a lit, foggy 3D miniature set, seen from above with a dreamy blur at the edges. Lamps cast real shadows and the light is the star.
keywords.when_to_use: Lovely for game-style trailers, cozy fantasy stories and atmospheric intros. Building the set takes time, so it suits a few rich scenes rather than many quick ones.
keywords.prompt_example: "15-second fantasy intro, pixel diorama animation, pixel characters in a foggy 3d miniature town, lanterns glowing, camera gliding above"

keywords.name: Pixel RPG
keywords.definition: A short film that looks and behaves like an old console role-playing game: a tiny pixel world in a limited palette, dialog boxes that type, menus, save screens and stat bars, where the whole palette shifting shows the mood.
keywords.when_to_use: Great for gaming content, nostalgic stories and playful tutorials framed as quests. The low resolution limits detail, so it is not for real products or faces.
keywords.prompt_example: "20-second story reel, pixel rpg animation, tiny hero walking through a pixel village, dialog box typing, palette shifting to sunset"

keywords.name: Pixiecore
keywords.definition: Small winged mischief: glitter, petals, dewdrops, and light that looks freshly enchanted.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for delicate magical scenes with a playful rather than grand tone.
keywords.prompt_example: "tiny pixie village in a teacup, pixiecore"

keywords.name: Plasma
keywords.definition: Glowing, electric gas that crackles in branching purple and pink threads, like inside a plasma ball. Alive with energy.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for sci-fi power, magic spells and electric moods. Dark backgrounds make the glowing threads stand out.
keywords.prompt_example: "plasma ball with purple electric threads, dark room"

keywords.name: Playful Learning App UI
keywords.definition: A bright, friendly app look with rounded shapes, chunky buttons with a thick bottom edge so they look pressable, cheerful mascot drawings and round Nunito type.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for learning apps, habit trackers, kids' tools and quiz games. Can feel too childish for professional software.
keywords.prompt_example: "lesson screen for a music learning app, playful learning app ui, chunky green buttons, owl mascot"

keywords.name: Plucky Sidekick
keywords.definition: The small, brave, loyal friend who follows the hero everywhere, ready with a joke or a rescue. Full of heart and a little bit clumsy.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for adventure and comedy scenes that need energy and warmth. Show them beside the hero so the role reads clearly.
keywords.prompt_example: "plucky sidekick fox riding on a knight's shoulder, sunny meadow"

keywords.name: Plus-Size
keywords.definition: A fuller, larger body shown naturally and confidently. AI tends to slim everyone down by default, so this word helps it show the many people who wear larger sizes.
keywords.when_to_use: Use whenever you want real, everyday representation in fashion, lifestyle and portrait scenes. Pair it with clothing and an activity so the person is the story, not their size.
keywords.prompt_example: "plus-size woman laughing with friends at a picnic, linen dress, sunny park"

keywords.name: Point of No Return
keywords.definition: The moment a character commits and can't go back: stepping off the cliff, closing the door behind them, crossing the bridge as it burns.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for brave, decisive moments in a story. Show what is being left behind as clearly as where they are going.
keywords.prompt_example: "point of no return, knight stepping onto a rope bridge as it frays, back to camera"

keywords.name: Polaroid
keywords.definition: An instant photo with a thick white border and soft, slightly faded colors. Creamy highlights, gentle blur and a real snapshot feeling.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for nostalgic, personal, party or road trip images. Say Polaroid photo with white frame if you want the border to show.
keywords.prompt_example: "Polaroid photo of friends at a beach bonfire, white frame"

keywords.name: Pop Kei
keywords.definition: Japanese street fashion in maximum color: toy accessories, layered rainbow, deliberate sensory overload.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for joy-loud fashion portraits and candy-colored chaos.
keywords.prompt_example: "street fashion portrait, pop kei style"

keywords.name: Pop Line Figures
keywords.definition: Simple figures drawn with thick, even black lines and flat bright colors, surrounded by little radiating motion lines so they look like they're dancing or buzzing.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for upbeat murals, music and party graphics, and any message about energy, love or togetherness.
keywords.prompt_example: "crowd of dancing figures with motion lines, pop line figures, bold black outlines, yellow background"

keywords.name: Post Conceptualism
keywords.definition: Idea-driven art after conceptualism: the concept matters, but craft is invited back.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for smart contemporary pieces balancing thought and object.
keywords.prompt_example: "installation of suspended letters, post-conceptualism"

keywords.name: Post-modernism
keywords.definition: Rule-breaking mashup of styles, eras, and irony; high art and pop culture in the same frame.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when you want deliberate stylistic collision and a wink.
keywords.prompt_example: "living room interior, postmodernism, 1980s"

keywords.name: Pottery Wheel
keywords.definition: Wet clay spinning under muddy hands as a bowl rises from the middle. Earthy, slow and very satisfying to watch.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for calm studio scenes and hands-at-work close-ups. A great pick for video, where the spinning clay really comes alive.
keywords.prompt_example: "hands shaping a clay bowl on a spinning pottery wheel, dusty studio light"

keywords.name: POV Shot
keywords.definition: The camera becomes a character's eyes; the audience wears their experience.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for immersion, horror peeks, and first-person storytelling.
keywords.prompt_example: "POV shot, hands opening the old journal"

keywords.name: Power Suit
keywords.definition: A bold suit made to command a room: strong padded shoulders, sharp lapels and a confident color like red, white or black. Very 1980s boardroom, still powerful today.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for leaders, bosses and confident portraits of any gender. Push it with a low angle for extra authority.
keywords.prompt_example: "woman in a red power suit with strong shoulders, glass boardroom"

keywords.name: Practical Lighting
keywords.definition: Scenes lit by sources visible in frame: lamps, neon signs, candles, screens.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for naturalistic night interiors and cozy realism.
keywords.prompt_example: "bar scene lit only by practicals, neon and lamps"

keywords.name: Preloader
keywords.definition: A full screen loading page that counts up to 100 percent, then slides away to reveal the website underneath.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it on portfolio or launch sites where a short, stylish entrance fits the mood. Keep it brief; making people wait for a pretty counter on every visit can annoy them.
keywords.prompt_example: "Add a preloader to my site: a dark screen with a big percentage counting to 100 and a progress bar, then it slides up to show the page."

keywords.name: Premium Product Web Design
keywords.definition: A refined product showcase with precise spacing, crisp Inter type, huge clean product photos and a polished, quietly expensive feel.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for gadgets, high-end products and launch pages. It relies on beautiful product images, and without them it looks empty.
keywords.prompt_example: "launch page for a cat energy drink can, premium product web design, one can on white, huge clean headline"

keywords.name: Preppy
keywords.definition: Collegiate polish: navy blazers, tennis whites, plaid and old-money tidiness.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for clean-cut lifestyle scenes and classic campus moods.
keywords.prompt_example: "picnic on a lawn, preppy aesthetic"

keywords.name: Presenter Explainer
keywords.definition: A cartoon host walks the viewer through the story on a paper-and-sticker page: she points at cards, stands inside the chart, and cuts to a big reaction close-up when the number lands.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for business, money and history explainers where a friendly guide keeps a voiceover personal and easy to follow.
keywords.prompt_example: "cartoon host in a yellow hoodie points at a bar chart on a cream dotted page, presenter explainer animation"

keywords.name: Pressed Flowers and Ink
keywords.definition: Real flattened flowers and leaves combined with ink drawing, so petals become a dress, hair or wings on a sketched figure.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for gentle, nature-filled art and botanical portraits. It works best on plain paper backgrounds, which keep it clean.
keywords.prompt_example: "ink sketch of a dancer with a skirt of pressed flowers"

keywords.name: Print Editorial Web Design
keywords.definition: A site laid out like a printed book or magazine, with neat columns, a clear grid and strong Oswald headlines over friendly Nunito body text.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for reports, online magazines, school projects and book sites. A little formal for playful apps.
keywords.prompt_example: "annual report website for a community garden, print editorial web design, two columns, big headlines"

keywords.name: Prism Effect
keywords.definition: Holding a glass prism in front of the lens to throw rainbows, ghostly double edges and soft color streaks across the picture.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for dreamy portraits and music photos with a touch of magic. Too much can hide the face, so ask for rainbows at the edge of the frame.
keywords.prompt_example: "portrait with prism effect, rainbow light streaks along the edge of the frame"

keywords.name: Product Mockup
keywords.definition: A clean, realistic picture showing a product, package or screen design in a real setting, like a box on a table or an app on a phone in someone's hand.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to preview packaging, labels and app screens before they exist. AI often garbles small text, so add real lettering afterward in a design app.
keywords.prompt_example: "product mockup of a plain kraft paper coffee bag on a marble counter, soft daylight"

keywords.name: Product Render
keywords.definition: A spotless studio shot of an object made in 3D, floating or sitting on a simple backdrop with clean, flattering light.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for packaging ideas, gadgets and mockups. Real logos and tiny printed text often come out garbled, so keep labels simple.
keywords.prompt_example: "wireless earbuds on a pastel pedestal, product render"

keywords.name: Professional Web Design
keywords.definition: A polished, business-ready site with modern Poppins type, structured sections and a trustworthy, organized look.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for shops, agencies, clinics and service businesses that want to look reliable. Safe, but not very memorable.
keywords.prompt_example: "website for an electronics repair shop, professional web design, blue and white, clear service cards"

keywords.name: Profile Shot
keywords.definition: The subject seen exactly side-on.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for silhouettes, faces deep in thought, or two people facing off.
keywords.prompt_example: "profile shot of him staring out of the train window"

keywords.name: Prussian Blue
keywords.definition: A deep, inky blue with a touch of green, made in Berlin around 1706. It is the blue of old blueprints and famous Japanese wave prints.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for rich night skies, ink art and moody seas. It can feel almost black in small images, so give it some light.
keywords.prompt_example: "stormy sea in prussian blue ink, woodblock print style"

keywords.name: Pulse Web Design
keywords.definition: A high-energy site with thick borders, striking geometric shapes, vivid oranges and other strong colors, and showy Limelight headlines that feel full of motion.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for sports, fitness, music and energy drink style launches. Too intense for calm or caring services.
keywords.prompt_example: "website for a spin class studio, pulse web design, thick borders, vivid orange shapes"

keywords.name: -punk
keywords.definition: From cyberpunk and steampunk, -punk means 'imagine a whole world powered by this.' Solarpunk runs on sunlight and gardens; steampunk runs on brass and steam.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to invent a world with its own technology and attitude. Pair it with a material or era so the AI knows what the world is built from.
keywords.prompt_example: "solarpunk village with rooftop gardens, bright morning"

keywords.name: Punk Zine Collage
keywords.definition: A homemade photocopied zine that builds itself: black and white cutouts, ransom-note letters and tape slap onto grainy paper, all a little crooked, with one loud accent color. Pieces jump in with choppy, hand-placed steps instead of smooth slides.
keywords.when_to_use: Great for bold, cheeky reels, ads and hot takes that want attitude. Too noisy for calm or serious topics, and it falls apart if you use more than one accent color.
keywords.prompt_example: "15-second reel, punk zine collage animation, photocopied cutouts and ransom letters slapping onto grainy paper, hot pink accent"

keywords.name: Purple Dashboard UI
keywords.definition: A clean app control center with a purple theme, navigation along the top bar, tidy cards and quick, developer-friendly screens.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for dashboards, hosting tools and team apps where people check on projects and push out updates. Not meant for marketing or storytelling pages.
keywords.prompt_example: "project control center for a web hosting app, purple dashboard ui, top bar menu, status cards"

keywords.name: Push In
keywords.definition: A gentle forward drift toward the subject, subtler than a full dolly move.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to quietly raise intensity inside dialogue or thought.
keywords.prompt_example: "slow push in as she hesitates over the phone"

keywords.name: Push-Through
keywords.definition: The camera pushes into something dark and round, like a peephole or a hole, and comes out in the next scene.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for curiosity, spy moods and down-the-rabbit-hole jumps.
keywords.prompt_example: "the camera pushes into the keyhole and comes out in the next room"

keywords.name: Qipao
keywords.definition: A fitted Chinese dress with a high mandarin collar, side slits and frog-knot buttons, often in silk with embroidered flowers. Also called a cheongsam.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for elegant portraits and 1930s Shanghai scenes. It is worn for weddings and Lunar New Year, so treat it as special dress, not a costume.
keywords.prompt_example: "woman in a red silk qipao, 1930s Shanghai street, soft evening light"

keywords.name: Quiet Aftermath
keywords.definition: The still moment after something big has happened. Confetti on an empty floor, smoke drifting over a field, a tired hero sitting in the dust.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when you want feeling without action, letting the viewer imagine what came before. Soft light and empty space make it stronger.
keywords.prompt_example: "quiet aftermath, empty ballroom at dawn, fallen streamers, one guest asleep"

keywords.name: Quiet Luxury
keywords.definition: Simple, expensive-looking clothes with no logos: cashmere knits, camel coats, soft trousers and perfect fit in cream, beige and grey. Rich without shouting about it.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for calm, upscale lifestyle and fashion images. It can look plain in a busy scene, so give it a clean, airy setting.
keywords.prompt_example: "woman in a cream cashmere sweater and camel coat, minimal sunlit apartment"

keywords.name: Quilting
keywords.definition: Blankets sewn from many fabric patches into patterns like stars, squares and zigzags, with soft puffy stitching.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for homey, nostalgic, warm scenes and colorful patterns. Also great as a style, like a quilted landscape.
keywords.prompt_example: "patchwork quilt of red and blue stars on a porch rocking chair"

keywords.name: Rack Focus
keywords.definition: Focus glides from one subject to another mid-shot, steering attention like a hand on the chin.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to connect two story elements without cutting.
keywords.prompt_example: "rack focus from the wilting rose to her face"

keywords.name: Raku
keywords.definition: Pottery pulled red hot from the kiln, leaving smoky black cracks, crackled white glaze and flashes of copper and rainbow sheen.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for earthy, dramatic pots with a lucky, unpredictable look. Every piece looks one of a kind.
keywords.prompt_example: "raku vase with copper flashes and smoky crackle, dark background"

keywords.name: Ramen Bowl
keywords.definition: A deep bowl of noodles in rich broth, topped with a soft egg, green onions and sliced pork. Warm and comforting in one look.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for cozy night-in scenes or late-night street food moods. Add steam rising to make it feel hot and fresh.
keywords.prompt_example: "ramen bowl, soft-boiled egg, steam rising, dark wooden counter"

keywords.name: Range Slider
keywords.definition: A bar with a round knob you drag left or right to pick a number. The bar fills in colour as you go and a little bubble shows the value.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it for settings with lots of in-between values, like brightness, volume or price. For exact numbers people may still want a box they can type into.
keywords.prompt_example: "Add a range slider for brightness from 0 to 100, with a pink filled track and a value bubble that follows the knob while I drag."

keywords.name: Rattan Peacock Chair
keywords.definition: A woven wicker chair with a giant fan-shaped back that frames whoever sits in it like a throne.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for boho portraits, 1970s glamour and tropical porches. Instantly makes a seated person the star.
keywords.prompt_example: "woman in a white dress seated in a rattan peacock chair, tropical porch"

keywords.name: Ray Tracing
keywords.definition: A 3D look where light bounces like it does in real life, giving true reflections in puddles, glass and shiny floors.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when reflections matter, like rainy streets, mirrors or chrome. It is a hint toward realism, not a magic fix for a weak prompt.
keywords.prompt_example: "rainy neon alley at night, ray tracing, reflections in puddles"

keywords.name: Rayograms
keywords.definition: Camera-less photography: objects laid on photosensitive paper, captured as ghostly silhouettes.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for elegant photogram-style compositions in white on black.
keywords.prompt_example: "botanicals as rayogram, white silhouettes on black"

keywords.name: Reaching Out
keywords.definition: An arm stretched toward something or someone: a hand reaching for a falling star, a friend, a door, a light. It makes the viewer feel the wanting.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for emotional moments of hope, rescue or longing. Show what they are reaching for, or the pose can feel unfinished.
keywords.prompt_example: "astronaut reaching out toward a floating flower, deep space glow"

keywords.name: Red Fox
keywords.definition: A slim fox with flame-orange fur, a white chest, black socks and a bushy tail. Clever, alert and gorgeous against snow or autumn leaves.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for storybook woodland scenes and wildlife portraits. It pops most against cool blue or green backgrounds.
keywords.prompt_example: "red fox in a frosty meadow at sunrise, golden hour"

keywords.name: Red Paper Cut
keywords.definition: Chinese red paper window cuts brought to life: jointed red cutouts laid on paper, where the cut is the drawing and the holes let the light through. Characters move in crisp steps, and one folded cut opens into a full rosette.
keywords.when_to_use: Lovely for festive greetings, new year posts and folk stories. It is very strongly linked to its tradition, so use it with respect and the right occasion.
keywords.prompt_example: "15-second new year greeting, red paper cut animation, a folded red paper opening into a lace rosette, a dragon cutout stepping across"

keywords.name: Refined Serif Web Design
keywords.definition: A carefully curated, minimal site with elegant Playfair Display serif type and understated, soft colors.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for boutique hotels, jewelers, weddings and fashion labels. Too delicate for loud, fun products.
keywords.prompt_example: "website for a wedding florist, refined serif web design, ivory and soft blush, elegant serif titles"

keywords.name: Reflection Shot
keywords.definition: The scene shown in a mirror, puddle, lake or shop window, sometimes upside down or doubled. Instant symmetry and a touch of mystery.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for clever compositions and calm, mirrored scenes. Say where the reflection is, like reflected in a puddle, for the best results.
keywords.prompt_example: "city lights reflected in a rain puddle, close to the ground, night"

keywords.name: Regency Era Fashion
keywords.definition: Early 1800s dress with a waistline just under the bust, light white muslin falling straight to the floor, short puffed sleeves, bonnets and little cropped jackets.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for period romance, country house scenes and garden walks. Say "empire waist" too if the waistline keeps slipping down.
keywords.prompt_example: "young woman in a white regency era muslin gown, walking through an english garden"

keywords.name: Relaxed Posture
keywords.definition: Loose shoulders, an easy stance and a body at rest, like someone leaning on a wall or settled into a chair. The opposite of stiff and posed.
keywords.when_to_use: Use to make people look comfortable and natural instead of mannequin-like. Add the action, like leaning or sitting, for the best results.
keywords.prompt_example: "young man in a relaxed posture leaning on a cafe counter, morning light"

keywords.name: Rembrandt
keywords.definition: (1606-1669) Dutch master of portraits glowing out of deep darkness. Warm golden light, brown shadows and faces full of feeling.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for moody, warm portraits lit by one strong light. His name is also a portrait lighting style in photography.
keywords.prompt_example: "portrait of an old scholar by candlelight, in the style of Rembrandt"

keywords.name: Retro 70s
keywords.definition: Warm oranges and browns, funky patterns, film grain, and sun-faded optimism.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for nostalgia, music culture, and warm analog vibes.
keywords.prompt_example: "retro 70s kitchen, orange tones, film grain"

keywords.name: Retro Arcade Maze Web Design
keywords.definition: A classic arcade game look with chunky Press Start 2P pixel lettering, dotted borders like a maze of little pellets, and bright, high-contrast colors on black.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for game sites, gaming events, retro snack brands and fun portfolios. Pixel fonts are hard to read in long sentences.
keywords.prompt_example: "high score page for a candy brand game, retro arcade maze web design, yellow dots on black, pixel text"

keywords.name: Retro Fairycore
keywords.definition: Fairycore filtered through 70s film: warm faded colors, vintage lace, sun-flare magic.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for nostalgic magical scenes that feel like an old photograph of something impossible.
keywords.prompt_example: "meadow picnic with fairies, retro fairycore, 70s film"

keywords.name: Retro Web Design
keywords.definition: A throwback site with vintage-inspired Macondo lettering, bold old-school color pairings and nostalgic touches like badges and stars.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for diners, record shops, barbers and brands with a nostalgic story. Can feel like a costume if the product is very modern.
keywords.prompt_example: "website for a roadside diner, retro web design, cherry red and cream, starburst badges"

keywords.name: Reveal
keywords.definition: The moment something hidden comes into view: a curtain pulled back, fog lifting from a castle, a face turning toward us. It is all about surprise.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for dramatic first looks and big moments. In video this shines with a slow camera move; in a still, show the hiding thing half moved.
keywords.prompt_example: "reveal, fog lifting from a giant sleeping dragon in a valley"

keywords.name: Richard Avedon
keywords.definition: (1923-2004) American fashion and portrait photographer known for people posed against plain white backgrounds. Sharp, direct and full of energy and personality.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for bold fashion portraits and striking faces on clean white. Not the right pick for moody or misty scenes.
keywords.prompt_example: "model mid-leap on a white backdrop, in the style of Richard Avedon, black and white"

keywords.name: Rim Light
keywords.definition: A thin outline of light around your subject's edges, like they're glowing from behind. Separates the subject from the background beautifully.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when your subject blends into the background, or you want a cinematic, polished feel.
keywords.prompt_example: "black cat on a fence, rim light, dusk"

keywords.name: Rim Lighting
keywords.definition: Light from behind traces a bright edge around the subject, carving them from the dark.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for silhouettes with definition and heroic or mysterious outlines.
keywords.prompt_example: "boxer in the dark, rim lighting on his shoulders"

keywords.name: Rinpa
keywords.definition: Classical Japanese decorative school: gold-leaf grounds, stylized waves and blossoms, flat elegance.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for decorative nature scenes with museum-grade Japanese styling.
keywords.prompt_example: "irises on gold leaf, rinpa style"

keywords.name: Ripple Click
keywords.definition: When you click a button, a soft circle spreads out from the exact spot you touched and fades away inside the button.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it to make buttons feel responsive and alive. Keep it subtle; a loud ripple on every small button gets tiring.
keywords.prompt_example: "Add a click ripple to my buttons: a soft white circle grows from where I click and fades out, staying inside the button."

keywords.name: Riso Web Design
keywords.definition: A joyful site that looks like a two-color risograph print (a grainy ink printer loved by zine makers), with warm off-white paper, fluorescent pink buttons and deep blue headings with a slightly offset print shadow.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for zines, art shops, small studios and indie events. The two-ink limit keeps it charming but leaves little room for big photo galleries.
keywords.prompt_example: "landing page for a candle shop, riso web design, pink and blue ink"

keywords.name: Risograph
keywords.definition: A grainy stencil printing look with bright see-through inks like fluoro pink and teal that overlap into new colors.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for zines, indie posters and playful illustrations with a soft, grainy texture. Fine detail can blur.
keywords.prompt_example: "risograph print of a cat in a plant shop, pink and teal ink"

keywords.name: Rococo
keywords.definition: Eighteenth-century French lightness: pastel palettes, curling ornament, flirtatious ease.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for airy aristocratic scenes and decorative softness.
keywords.prompt_example: "garden party painting, rococo style"

keywords.name: Rococo Revival
keywords.definition: Victorian-era rococo comeback: carved curves and ornament with heavier nineteenth-century polish.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for plush period interiors and ornate furniture scenes.
keywords.prompt_example: "parlor interior, rococo revival furniture"

keywords.name: Romantic Academia
keywords.definition: Academia aesthetic warmed with poetry and longing: handwritten letters, roses on old books.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for soft scholarly scenes where the library is also a love story.
keywords.prompt_example: "desk with letters and roses, romantic academia"

keywords.name: Rooftop Night Two-Shot
keywords.definition: Two people on a rooftop at night, the camera drifting between each face and a shot of both together.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it for quiet night scenes between two characters. City lights behind them do a lot of the work, so mention them.
keywords.prompt_example: "two friends on a rooftop at night, city lights behind, the camera drifting between each face and the two-shot"

keywords.name: Rose Gold
keywords.definition: Gold mixed with copper to give a warm, pinkish blush color. Softer and more romantic than yellow gold.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for jewelry, watches and product shots with a warm, modern, gentle feel. Pairs nicely with pastel backgrounds.
keywords.prompt_example: "rose gold bangle with tiny diamonds on blush pink silk"

keywords.name: Rosemary
keywords.definition: A woody herb with needle-like, silvery green leaves and tiny pale blue flowers. Rustic and fresh, like a cottage kitchen.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for herb gardens, rustic kitchen still lifes and cooking scenes. Small sprigs make a nice garnish detail in food shots.
keywords.prompt_example: "rosemary sprigs on a wooden board with sea salt and olive oil"

keywords.name: Rotoscope
keywords.definition: Animation traced over real filmed movement, so drawn characters move with lifelike weight and grace. It sits halfway between live action and drawing.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when you want drawn characters that move naturally, like a dancer or a runner. In video, expect a slightly wobbly, dreamy line.
keywords.prompt_example: "woman dancing in a kitchen, rotoscope animation, bold outlines"

keywords.name: Rough Sketch Line Drawing
keywords.definition: Loose, energetic pencil or ink lines that look mid-thought; construction lines welcome.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for concept-art energy or when polish would kill the charm.
keywords.prompt_example: "rough sketch line drawing of a dancer"

keywords.name: Rubber Hose Animation
keywords.definition: The bouncy cartoon style of the 1920s and 30s, where arms and legs bend like noodles with no elbows or knees. Think pie-cut eyes, white gloves and big grins.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for cheerful, old-timey characters with lots of bounce. It looks most like itself in black and white or faded color.
keywords.prompt_example: "dancing teapot character, rubber hose animation, black and white"

keywords.name: Rubber Hose Ragtime
keywords.definition: A scratchy old-time ink cartoon where characters, props and even buildings bounce to a jaunty band. Arms and legs swing like garden hoses with no elbows, and scenes close on a shrinking circle.
keywords.when_to_use: Great for playful intros, music-driven ads and retro-themed shorts. Everything bounces all the time, so it can feel too goofy for serious messages.
keywords.prompt_example: "10-second intro, rubber hose ragtime cartoon, bouncy black and white characters dancing on the beat, iris out"

keywords.name: Running Toward Camera
keywords.definition: Your subject racing straight at the viewer, hair and clothes flying, getting bigger in the frame. It pulls you right into the action.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for chases, joyful reunions and big action. It is strongest in video; in a still image, add motion blur so it doesn't look frozen.
keywords.prompt_example: "kids running toward camera through a sprinkler, summer afternoon, slow motion"

keywords.name: Rush-By Shot
keywords.definition: A low camera with a wide lens races right past the subject.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it for pure speed. The wide lens makes the rush feel even faster, but fine detail can blur.
keywords.prompt_example: "a wide-lens camera at knee height hurtles past a skateboarder, who swings across the frame, horizon rolling"

keywords.name: SaaS Flat Illustration
keywords.definition: Friendly, simple vector drawings used on software websites: flat colors, rounded people with no fine detail, floating charts, cloud icons and laptops.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for websites, onboarding screens and explainer graphics. It can feel generic, so pick a brand-like color palette to make it yours.
keywords.prompt_example: "saas flat illustration of a team building a dashboard together, purple and teal palette, white background"

keywords.name: Sage Green
keywords.definition: A soft, gray-green, like the leaves of the sage plant. Calm, earthy and easy on the eyes.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for calm interiors, wedding themes and natural, gentle looks. It is quiet on purpose, so it will not grab attention.
keywords.prompt_example: "sage green kitchen with brass handles, morning light"

keywords.name: Salvage Art
keywords.definition: Art from rescued materials: driftwood, scrap metal, and discards given second lives.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for eco-craft sculpture concepts and weathered assemblage.
keywords.prompt_example: "whale sculpture from driftwood, salvage art"

keywords.name: Sandro Botticelli
keywords.definition: (c. 1445-1510) Italian Renaissance painter of graceful goddesses with flowing hair, floating fabrics and flower-strewn gardens. Pale, light colors and elegant lines.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for romantic, mythical, springtime figures. It shines with flowers and flowing hair, less so with modern scenes.
keywords.prompt_example: "goddess with flowing red-gold hair in a flower meadow, in the style of Sandro Botticelli"

keywords.name: Sari
keywords.definition: A long, unstitched length of cloth, usually five to nine yards, draped around the body over a fitted blouse, with the decorated end falling over the shoulder. Worn across South Asia in many regional styles.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for everyday portraits, festivals and weddings. Richly woven silk saris, often red, are bridal wear in many regions, so name the occasion and color you want.
keywords.prompt_example: "woman in a deep red silk sari with gold border, marigold garlands, warm evening light"

keywords.name: Saul Leiter
keywords.definition: (1923-2013) American photographer who shot New York in soft, painterly color. Think red umbrellas in snow, blurry shapes through fogged windows and shy little pops of color.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for dreamy, rainy, colorful city moments with lots of layers. If you want sharp and clear, pick someone else.
keywords.prompt_example: "red umbrella in falling snow seen through a steamy cafe window, in the style of Saul Leiter"

keywords.name: Scale Contrast
keywords.definition: Something tiny placed against something enormous.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it to show size, power or loneliness. It works best when the small thing is easy to spot, so give it a bright colour or a clear outline.
keywords.prompt_example: "scale contrast, a tiny robot standing beneath a giant dam wall"

keywords.name: Scandinavian Interior
keywords.definition: Bright white walls, pale wood floors, simple furniture, cozy wool throws and plenty of daylight. Clean and homey at the same time.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for fresh, light, lived-in rooms. A safe, friendly default that rarely goes wrong.
keywords.prompt_example: "Scandinavian interior kitchen, white walls, birch table, winter daylight"

keywords.name: Sci-Fi Sitcom Toon
keywords.definition: A grown-up sci-fi cartoon: thick dark outlines that never stop wiggling, flat colors with hard shadows, a deadpan hero and a panicking sidekick, and a glowing portal that jumps them between worlds, each in its own colors.
keywords.when_to_use: Fun for comedy skits, dialogue-driven reels and quirky brand stories. It lives on writing and timing, so it falls flat without a funny script.
keywords.prompt_example: "20-second comedy skit, sci-fi sitcom toon animation, deadpan character and panicking sidekick stepping through a glowing green portal"

keywords.name: Scientific Poster
keywords.definition: The big printed poster researchers pin up at conferences: a title banner across the top, neat columns, charts, photos and small blocks of text.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for research mockups, school projects and conference scenes. AI can't write accurate science text, so treat it as a layout idea and fill in real words yourself.
keywords.prompt_example: "scientific poster about coral reefs, title banner, charts and photos in neat columns"

keywords.name: Scrapbooking
keywords.definition: Pages layered with photos, washi tape, ticket stubs, pressed flowers and handwritten notes. A happy, collected mess of memories.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for nostalgic flat lays, journaling vibes, or a memory-board look. Any written words may come out garbled, so keep the text small or skip it.
keywords.prompt_example: "scrapbook page with polaroids, washi tape and pressed flowers, flat lay"

keywords.name: Screen Print
keywords.definition: Flat, bold layers of ink pushed through a mesh screen. Bright solid colors, slightly off-register edges, like gig posters and pop art.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for poppy posters, t-shirt graphics and bold portraits. Limit to a few colors for the most believable look.
keywords.prompt_example: "screen print poster of a surfer, three colors, slightly misaligned"

keywords.name: Screentone
keywords.definition: The dotty grey shading in black and white manga, made from patterns of tiny printed dots. It adds shadow and tone without any color.
keywords.when_to_use: Use when you want the feel of a real printed manga page. It only makes sense in black and white or very limited color.
keywords.prompt_example: "manga page, girl on a train at dusk, screentone shading"

keywords.name: Scroll Pinning
keywords.definition: A section freezes in place while you keep scrolling, and its inside changes step by step, like a slideshow you drive with the scroll wheel. When the steps are done, the page moves on.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it to walk people through a process or a product story in clear steps. It can feel like the page is stuck if the steps take too long, so keep it to three or four.
keywords.prompt_example: "Pin the How it works section while I scroll and swap through steps 01, 02 and 03, then let the page continue"

keywords.name: Scroll Progress Bar
keywords.definition: A thin coloured bar across the top of the page grows from empty to full as you read down. It shows at a glance how much of the article is left.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it on blog posts, guides and long articles so readers know how far they have come. It adds little on short pages.
keywords.prompt_example: "Add a thin pink bar across the top of my article that fills up as the reader scrolls"

keywords.name: Scroll Snap
keywords.definition: The page is made of full-screen panels, and each scroll glides to the next one and settles exactly on it. You never stop halfway between two panels.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it for story pages, product tours or galleries where each screen is one idea. It can feel bossy on pages with lots of reading, so save it for short, visual sections.
keywords.prompt_example: "Make my page a stack of full-height panels that snap into place one at a time as I scroll"

keywords.name: Seascape
keywords.definition: The ocean as the subject: waves, horizon, weather, and light on water.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for calm, power, or loneliness. The mood of the water is the mood of the image.
keywords.prompt_example: "stormy seascape with a distant lighthouse"

keywords.name: Segmented Control
keywords.definition: A pill split into a few side by side choices, with a coloured highlight that slides to the one you pick. Only one choice is on at a time.
keywords.when_to_use: Use it to switch between two to four views of the same thing, like Day, Week and Month. With more options, use a dropdown menu instead.
keywords.prompt_example: "Add a segmented control with Day, Week and Month where a pink highlight slides between them and the chart below updates"

keywords.name: Seigaiha
keywords.definition: Overlapping half circles stacked like fish scales, each one a little wave. A traditional Japanese pattern meaning calm seas and good luck.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for kimonos, wrapping paper, tiles and calm ocean themes. Ask for gold or indigo lines to keep it looking refined.
keywords.prompt_example: "seigaiha wave pattern, gold lines on deep indigo"

keywords.name: Serene
keywords.definition: Deep calm. Still water, soft light, nothing rushing anywhere.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for wellness, nature, and breathing room. The antidote to busy images.
keywords.prompt_example: "serene mountain lake at dawn, mist rising"

keywords.name: Sfumato
keywords.definition: Soft, smoky blending where edges melt into shadow with no hard lines. A Renaissance painting method that gives faces a hushed, mysterious glow.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for gentle, timeless portraits and quiet moods. It softens everything, so it's not the pick for crisp detail.
keywords.prompt_example: "portrait of a young scholar, sfumato, warm dim light"

keywords.name: Shadow Art
keywords.definition: A pile of random objects that casts a shadow of something totally different, like a heap of junk making the shadow of a dancer.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for surprising reveals and clever art pieces. The AI may struggle to match the shadow, so keep the shadow shape simple.
keywords.prompt_example: "pile of old shoes casting a shadow of a cat on the wall"

keywords.name: Shadow Puppet Animation
keywords.definition: A shadow theatre in a warm lamp-lit room: black jointed puppets move across a glowing paper screen, swinging on their joints, blurring as they step away from the screen and flickering softly in the light.
keywords.when_to_use: Lovely for folk tales, bedtime stories and moody storytelling. Faces and small details do not show in silhouette, so it suits simple shapes and clear actions.
keywords.prompt_example: "20-second folk tale, shadow puppet animation, black jointed fox and bird puppets moving across a glowing amber paper screen"

keywords.name: Shaker Furniture
keywords.definition: Plain, beautifully made wooden furniture from an American religious community: ladderback chairs, peg rails and simple cabinets with no decoration.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for calm, honest, handmade rooms. Very quiet, so pair it with soft daylight.
keywords.prompt_example: "Shaker ladderback chairs and peg rail, plain wooden room, window light"

keywords.name: Shallow Depth of Field
keywords.definition: Razor-thin focus: the subject is sharp, the world melts into blur.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for portrait intimacy and isolating subjects from busy backgrounds.
keywords.prompt_example: "shallow depth of field, her face sharp, cafe dissolved behind"

keywords.name: Shattering Glass
keywords.definition: Glass breaking into a burst of sharp, glittering shards, either frozen in midair or flying outward. Instant drama.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for action, product shots and big surprise moments. Hands and faces close to the shards can come out messy, so give them space.
keywords.prompt_example: "perfume bottle shattering, glass shards frozen midair, black background"

keywords.name: Sheet Music
keywords.definition: Pages of musical notes on lined staffs, often aged and curling at the edges. Romantic and a little old-world.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for vintage still lifes, romantic scenes and paper-texture backgrounds. The notes will not be real music, so do not count on readable melodies.
keywords.prompt_example: "old sheet music on a piano, dried roses, candlelight"

keywords.name: Sherlock Holmes
keywords.definition: The sharp-eyed detective from the original stories, tall and thin with a hawk-like nose, as first drawn in old magazine illustrations with a deerstalker cap and travelling cape. Ask for the book version, not later screen versions.
keywords.when_to_use: Use for Victorian mysteries, foggy London streets and clever detective portraits. Mention 'Victorian illustration' to keep him true to the books.
keywords.prompt_example: "sherlock holmes examining a muddy footprint with a magnifying glass, foggy gaslit london, victorian illustration"

keywords.name: Shonen Style
